Key prior results: N (total specifications) = 15,840; 7,561 specifications produced a claim. Claim flip rate F = 73.2% (probability two distinct specifications yield different structured Annex IV statements). Standardising the evaluation metric: flip rate = 59.4%. Holding circuit size fixed (removing size from claim): flip rate = 27.1%. Modal claim share π* = 41.1%. Median circuit overlap (Jaccard) ≈ 4%. Functional agreement (adjusted for chance via Cohen’s kappa) ≈ 0. One documented discovery objective failed to execute; seven objectives documented, six executed. Study limited to GPT-2 small on the indirect-object-identification canonical task; one unrun replication (Pythia-160m). Pre-registered hypotheses: H2 requires F > 0.20 with CI lower bound above 0.20; H3: result not separated from the random null; H4: F - (1 - agreement) > 0.10. Bootstrap: B = 10,000 resamples of specifications (not pairs), conditional on the declared grid; random-null multiverses R = 1,000. Definitions/decisions from glossary to retain: circuit = discovered subset of model edges; circuit discovery returns C(s) for specification s; claim map φ is deterministic code mapping a circuit to a structured Annex IV statement (φ_overseer and φ_affected); claim classes c and modal share π* = max_c n_c/N; filability: evidence filable at tolerance α iff π* ≥ 1−α; COARSE/MEDIUM/FINE are nested claim granularities; size classes labelled distributed/moderate/sparse and produced by calibration rule from a measured node-count curve; selected circuit size is transformed by log10 for REML variance decomposition. Metrics: Jaccard similarity ̅J, circuit instability D = 1−Jaccard, F = claim flip rate, U-statistic form for F and ̅J (pairs share specifications). P0: pre-registered premise for which mean Jaccard is reported but not tested.

Study tests whether circuit-derived regulatory statements survive defensible analytic variation. Pre-registered crossed grid of seven analytic axes (levels from published implementations); deterministic claim map φ converts each discovered circuit to a structured Annex IV statement. N = 15,840 specifications; 7,561 produced a claim. Claim flip rate F = 73.2% (95% CI 0.725–0.738). Modal claim share π* = 41.1% (fails filability at any plausible tolerance since π* < 1−α for typical α). Standardising the evaluation metric yields F = 59.4%. Removing circuit size from claim and holding size fixed yields F = 27.1% (95% CI 0.255–0.286), which exceeds the pre-registered H2 threshold (H2: F > 0.20 with CI lower bound > 0.20). Circuits are structurally near-disjoint: median pairwise Jaccard ≈ 4%. Functional agreement (Cohen’s kappa) ≈ 0.015, indicating functions not just reworded. One of seven documented discovery objectives failed to execute (six executed). Study limited to GPT-2 small on the indirect-object-identification canonical task (one unrun replication planned on Pythia-160m). Bootstrap and inferential details (from earlier parts): B = 10,000 resamples of specifications conditional on grid; random-null multiverses R = 1,000. Key metrics/definitions retained: circuit = subset of model edges C(s); claim classes c; modal share π* = max_c n_c/N; Jaccard ȷ̅ and instability D = 1−Jaccard. P0 (pre-registered premise) reports mean Jaccard but is not hypothesis-tested.

Introduction frames regulatory need for consistent conclusions across analysts; cites EU Regulation (consolidated/amended text read 11 Aug 2026). Mechanistic interpretability (circuit discovery) proposed as technical content; study asks whether circuit-derived Annex IV regulatory statements survive defensible analytic variation and gives a decision rule for standards bodies. Pre-registered crossed grid (multiverse) of 7 analytic axes; every level from published implementations; deterministic map φ converts discovered circuits to structured Annex IV statements. Filability criterion: π* ≥ 1−α (π* = modal claim share, α = permitted disagreement). Key reported results (from earlier parts): N = 15,840 specifications, 7,561 produced a claim; claim flip rate F = 73.2% (95% CI 0.725–0.738); modal claim share π* = 41.1% (fails filability for typical α). Standardising the evaluation metric yields F = 59.4%. Removing circuit size from claim and holding size fixed yields F = 27.1% (95% CI 0.255–0.286), which exceeds pre-registered H2 (H2: F > 0.20 with CI LB > 0.20). Circuits structurally near-disjoint (median pairwise Jaccard ≈ 4%; P0 reported mean Jaccard but not hypothesis-tested); functional agreement low (Cohen’s κ ≈ 0.015). One of seven discovery objectives failed to execute (six executed). Study limited to GPT-2 small on an indirect-object-identification canonical task; planned unrun replication on Pythia-160m. Inferential details: B = 10,000 bootstrap resamples conditional on grid; random-null multiverses R = 1,000. Contribution list also warns pooled statistics can invert when object sizes differ and states they show three such inversions.

Related work grounds the paper's premises and methods. Key points: (1) Non-identifiability: Méloux et al. show behaviours need not have unique mechanistic explanations; that is taken as the paper’s premise. (2) Faithfulness metric sensitivity: Miller et al. find ablation-based faithfulness scores sensitive to analyst choices; the authors use Miller’s released library and expand from one axis to a pre-registered crossed grid of 7 analytic axes. (3) Structure vs function: Bayat Makou et al. report “phantom specialisation” (structurally distinct circuits implementing the same computation) — the strongest objection to the study design; the paper asserts Section 7.6 uses functional measurement and finds the discovered circuits are not functionally interchangeable. (4) Variance/estimation: Méloux et al. (other paper) frame mechanistic interpretability as estimation; seed variance is one axis of the multiverse. (5) Auditability: calls for auditing/standardised evaluation motivate the regulatory criterion. (6) Multiverse/specification-curve literature (Steegen/Simonsohn/Simmons) supplies the analytic-flexibility framework used. (7) Explanation metrics under optimization: Hsia et al. show sufficiency and comprehensiveness can be inflated without changing predictions; these are two of the paper’s four evaluation metrics, so the authors report discard rates by metric rather than pooling. This section contains no numerical results or tables.

Related-work and premises: non-identifiability (Méloux et al.); faithfulness metrics sensitive to analyst choices (Miller et al.) — authors use Miller's library and expand to a pre-registered crossed grid of 7 analytic axes; phantom specialization (Bayat Makou) motivates functional checks (Section 7.6); mechanistic interpretability framed as estimation (seed variance an axis); calls for auditability/regulatory criteria; multiverse/specification-curve framework used; Hsia et al. warn sufficiency/comprehensiveness can be inflated, so authors report discard rates by metric rather than pooling. Key quantitative claims from this part: discovered circuits are more stable than a size-matched random null at fixed circuit size: flip/flip-rate 0.2746 (discovered) vs 0.4230 (random) (Section 7.5). Functional instability (1 − per-example agreement between circuits) = 0.3972 pooled, 0.4777 at smallest circuits (text; pooled also appears in Section 7.6). Cohen’s kappa = 0.0146 (Section 7.6) — interpreted as circuits functionally uncorrelated. Seed selection pertains to sampled prompts (evaluation-set variability), not nondeterminism; scope limited to one model, one task (Sections 6 and 9). Keep these section pointers and numeric values for cross-checks with results/tables in later parts.

errors.evidence: "Equation 2: F=1-\frac{\sum_c n_c(n_c-1)}{N(N-1)}." (this part) and the quoted ceiling: "The stated ceiling is F\leq1-1/k, where k is the number of claim classes." (this part).

Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Pre-registered crossed design for GPT-2 small (Q7V) on indirect-object identification (Z4K); committed but unrun second-model plan: Pythia-160m (M9B). Deterministic code G7U maps discovered circuits to structured Annex IV statements; 7,561 claim-producing specifications; pairwise claim disagreement F = 0.7316 (pooled). Removing size from statements and conditioning on size reduces disagreement to 0.2706. Discovered circuits outperform size-matched random null (A6N) at fixed size; pooled comparison reverses. Graph: factorised (query/key/value) with |E| = 32,491 edges; 12 blocks, 12 heads/block (144 heads), 12 MLPs. Specification s = (objective o, ablation operator a, corruption distribution d, metric m, size threshold τ, prompt variant P, seed r, granularity g). Ablation operators: 7 total (five read corruption, two do not); d nested within operators that read corruption. Granularities: COARSE (E7R), MEDIUM (K8Z), FINE (V2H). Metrics (four): comprehensiveness (T9V), KL divergence (H2W), logit difference (N6C), sufficiency (U4J). Discovery: crossed grid, discovery cell counted before metric/threshold/statement reporting; metric-relative threshold rule; retention/discard rates tracked; one objective arm failed (MSE/integral target runtime error). Statistical tooling: Jaccard α = intersection/union, α-bar = mean over unordered pairs; D = 1 - Jaccard; F defined in Gini–Simpson form (pair disagreement); G and F_within(G) for conditioning; pi* = max_class_share; Y3W filability requires pi* >= 1 - alpha (alpha = filing tolerance). Nulls: R = 1,000 null multiverses; null degeneracy = collapse. Inference: bootstrap B = 10,000 resamples of specifications; pairwise U-statistics for F and α-bar; p-values not reported (grid not independent). Functional diagnostics: agreement, functional instability = 1 - agreement, functional gap = F - (1 - agreement), Cohen's kappa, accuracy. Structural variance: REML over log10(size). Discovery families: edge-attribution patching (R8X), integrated edge gradients (B3Q); optimal ablation (C4Y) unsupported. Pre-registration artifacts: deviations file, six-cell validation slice, environment fingerprint, content-addressed git tree, tag 'prereg-p1-confirmatory'. GPU not required.

final_notes: Key outcomes: Registered outcomes include J6D (P0)=0.1396 [0.1377,0.1418]; X4R (H2) F=0.7316 [0.7247,0.7380] (threshold 0.20, confirmed); Q2F (H3) flagged (Table3 decision-rule contradiction); Z8N (H4) gap F-(1-agreement)=0.3344 [0.3297,0.3394]. Data: 15,840 realized experiments; 8,279 discarded (no circuit, ~52.3%); 7,561 kept specs; 3,218 distinct circuits; 28,580,580 spec pairs. D quantiles: 1%=0.196, 25%=0.788, median=0.960, 75%=0.998. Median shared-edge ≈4%; median circuit size ≈200 edges. Sec7.2 pair disagreement 73.2% (CI ≈0.725–0.738). Modal class early/distributed 3,107 (41.09%); size-agg early/late/middle 47.9%/43.6%/8.5%. Sec7.3 ablations: evaluation-metric standardisation had largest effect; Table 6 residual F=0.5939 (95% CI 0.5803–0.6063). Sec7.4 fixed-size: F≈0.2706 (CI 0.2550–0.2859). Sec7.5 random-baseline comparisons: pooled discovered 0.7316 vs random(A6N) 0.6774; fixed-size K8Z discovered 0.2746 vs random 0.4230; fixed-size E7R discovered 0.2706 vs random 0.3822. Sec7.6 diagnostics: pooled per-example agreement 0.6028 → pooled F=0.3972; smallest-circuit F=0.4777; pooled Cohen's kappa 0.0146; per-size kappa 0.016–0.047; raw agreement 0.52–0.92; accuracy 0.51–0.95; 6/10 sizes fail gap threshold; 5 sizes have negative gap; pooled gap band 500–2,000 edges. Sec8 protocol: report π*, F, discard rates, within-group decompositions; pass if π* ≥ 1−α. Sec9 limitations: one-model/one-task, planned second-model unrun, size treated as outcome (affects F/gap sign), limited multiverse, high/uneven discard, small-group bootstrap invalid. Sec10 discussion: documents instrument execution/discard issues (220 failed objective cells; 8,279 specs no circuit; 52.3% discard) and notes pooled vs fixed-size baseline conflict. Sec11 (Reproducibility): public tag 'prereg-p1-confirmatory'; archive verification across all 1,320 confirmatory cells; content-addressed comparison finds 22/22 files identical; analysis needs no GPU; one script recomputes headline quantities (36 checks, 0 failures; F checked via three routes including brute-force pairs); another checks every manuscript numeric token; tables emitted directly; test suite contains 343 tests.

Title: "Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability" (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Study question: do circuit-derived regulatory claims remain compatible across defensible analytic settings. Design: pre-registered crossed design using published implementations to discover circuits for GPT-2 small on indirect object identification. Code: deterministic conversion of circuits into structured "Annex IV" statements. Scope: one model (GPT-2 small) and one task (indirect object identification); a planned second-model study remains unrun. Key quantities/results: 7,561 claim-producing specifications; overall pairwise claim disagreement = 0.7316. Claim: "No single-axis standardisation permits filing under the registered tolerances." Alternative comparison: removing size from statements and conditioning comparisons on size reduces disagreement to 0.2706. Functional results: discovered circuits outperform size-matched randomness at fixed size, which reverses the pooled (unconditioned) comparison; however, functional measurements do not support treating circuits as interchangeable mechanisms. Note: "Size conditioning also qualifies the pooled functional-gap result." Glossary section begins but is not provided in this part.

Title: "Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability". Question: do circuit-derived regulatory claims remain compatible across defensible analytic settings. Design: pre-registered crossed/grid design (confirmatory sweep) for Q7V (GPT-2 small) on Z4K (indirect object identification); planned second-model (M9B Pythia-160m) unrun. Deterministic claim-map G7U converts circuits to Annex IV statements; filability criterion Y3W requires π* ≥ 1−α. Key counts/results (from earlier parts): 7,561 claim-producing specifications; overall pairwise claim disagreement F = 0.7316; size-conditioning reduces pooled disagreement to 0.2706; discovered circuits outperform size-matched random null when conditioned on size but pooled functional comparison reverses; functional gap computed and size-conditioning affects it. Graph and notation: factorised graph with separate query/key/value; edge set E with |E| = 32,491. Model: 12 blocks (b), 12 heads per block → 144 heads total; 12 MLPs. Specification s = (o, a, d, m, τ, P, r, g) where a = ablation operator (7 operators: 5 read corruption, 2 do not), d nested in operators that read corruption, r samples prompts (evaluation-set variability), g = granularity (COARSE E7R reported with/without size term, MEDIUM K8Z, FINE V2H). Circuit comparison metrics: D(s_i,s_j)=1−|C_i∩C_j|/|C_i∪C_j|; Jaccard similarity ̅J averaged over unordered pairs; F is pair disagreement (Gini–Simpson form). Nulls and inference: A6N size-matched random null sampling full edge population, R=1000 null multiverses; bootstrap B=10,000 resamples of specifications; pairwise U-statistics used; REML for size-variance decomposition on log10(size). Functional definitions: functional agreement, functional instability =1−agreement, functional gap = F − (1−agreement); Cohen's kappa and accuracy reported. One objective arm failed (MSE/integral target runtime error); deviations file and environment fingerprint recorded; prereg commit 'prereg-p1-confirmatory'; GPU not required.

errors.claim: "Note the ceiling: F\leq 1-1/k for k claim classes, so a reported flip rate must be read against the number of classes the map can produce. With the nine classes observed here the ceiling is 0.8889, and the observed 0.7316 is 82.3% of it. F is not near one by construction."
errors.evidence: "Equation 2: F = 1 - \frac{\sum_{c} n_{c}(n_{c}-1)}{N(N-1)}" (the finite-sample Gini–Simpson form) and the quoted ceiling sentence above.
errors.explanation: The displayed formula for F is the without-replacement (finite-sample) form; in fact F = (N/(N-1))*(1 - \sum_c p_c^2). The maximum over distributions p_c (uniform p_c=1/k) gives F_max = (N/(N-1))*(1 - 1/k), which can exceed 1 - 1/k for finite N (and equals 1 when N=k and each class has n_c=1). Thus the statement "F \le 1-1/k" is mathematically incorrect for the estimator in Eq.2.

Paper: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Research question: whether mechanistic/circuit discovery evidence is robust to defensible analytic variation (two competent analysts, same system and tool, different defensible settings). Method: pre-registered crossed grid of 7 analytic axes (levels taken from published implementations); mapped each discovered circuit via a deterministic claim map to a structured Annex IV statement. Dataset/experiment: GPT-2 small on an indirect object identification task; 15,840 pre-registered specifications, of which 7,561 produced a claim. Main results: derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs (95% CI 0.725–0.738); modal claim covers 41.1% of the space. Standardising the most influential axis (evaluation metric) yields flip rate 59.4%. Removing circuit size from the claim and holding it fixed yields flip rate 27.1% (95% CI 0.255–0.286), still above the pre-registered threshold (threshold value not given here). Circuits are near-disjoint (median pairwise Jaccard overlap 4%) and functionally uncorrelated (Cohen's kappa 0.015) — authors argue instability is not merely one mechanism restated. They provide a filability criterion/protocol and report one of seven documented discovery objectives fails to execute on the library's canonical task. Study limitation: single model and single task; generalisability untested.

errors.claim: "Note the ceiling: F\leq 1-1/k for k claim classes, so a reported flip rate must be read against the number of classes the map can produce. With the nine classes observed here the ceiling is 0.8889, and the observed 0.7316 is 82.3% of it. F is not near one by construction."
errors.evidence: "Equation 2: F = 1 - \frac{\sum_{c} n_{c}(n_{c}-1)}{N(N-1)}" (the finite-sample Gini–Simpson form) and the quoted ceiling sentence above.
errors.explanation: The displayed formula for F is the without-replacement (finite-sample) form; in fact F = (N/(N-1))*(1 - \sum_c p_c^2). The maximum over distributions p_c (uniform p_c=1/k) gives F_max = (N/(N-1))*(1 - 1/k), which can exceed 1 - 1/k for finite N (and equals 1 when N=k and each class has n_c=1). Thus the statement "F \le 1-1/k" is mathematically incorrect for the estimator in Eq.2.

steps.notes_before: Specification tuple s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). Circuit discovery returns C(s) ⊆ E; for GPT-2 small (factorised graph, separate q/k/v) |E|=32,491. Architecture counts: 12 layers × 12 heads = 144 attention heads, plus 12 MLPs (156 components). Circuit instability: D(s_i,s_j)=1 - |C_i ∩ C_j|/|C_i ∪ C_j| (Jaccard distance); \bar{J} mean Jaccard similarity. Claim instability: φ maps circuits → Annex IV classes. Flip rate F given by Eq.2: F = 1 - Σ_c n_c(n_c-1)/[N(N-1)] (unbiased Gini–Simpson estimator); modal share π* = max_c n_c/N. Within-group form F_within(G) given by Eq.3. Filability: evidence filable at tolerance α iff π* ≥ 1-α. Internal inconsistency found: the part asserts a ceiling F ≤ 1 - 1/k (numerical ceiling 0.8889 for k=9), but Eq.2 implies a finite-sample scaling F_max = (N/(N-1))(1 - 1/k) which can exceed 1 - 1/k (and can reach 1 if N=k and n_c=1). errors.claim: One-axis standardisation is insufficient: metric removes 0.1377 from 0.7316, leaving 0.5939, CI 0.5803 to 0.6063 (Table 6, Evaluation metric).
errors.evidence: Earlier reported values in my notes: P0 mean Jaccard J̄ = 0.1396 [0.1377, 0.1418]. H2 pooled discovered flip rate F = 0.7316 [0.7247, 0.7380].
errors.explanation: The part subtracts 0.1377 (the lower CI bound of J̄) from 0.7316 to get 0.5939, but the paper elsewhere reports J̄'s mean as 0.1396. Arithmetic: 0.7316 - 0.1396 = 0.5920 (not 0.5939). Using the reported CIs, the difference CI would plausibly be ~[0.7247 - 0.1418, 0.7380 - 0.1377] ≈ [0.5829, 0.6003], which does not match the stated [0.5803, 0.6063]. The part therefore uses inconsistent numbers (and does not clarify that it subtracted a CI bound rather than the mean).

errors.claim: Six alternatives exceed the committed result, including halving thresholds.
errors.evidence: First paragraph asserts: 'Six alternatives exceed the committed result, including halving thresholds.' Later the same part's 'Claims and evidence' says: 'Four alternatives exceed the committed result: Table 1, “committed bins” 0.7316; “all thresholds × 0.5” 0.7448; “× 0.8” 0.7435; “× 0.9” 0.7394; “deciles” 0.7719.' Only four alternative binnings (×0.5, ×0.8, ×0.9, deciles) have F > 0.7316.

errors.claim: The grid contains seven objectives, seven operators, four corruption distributions nested within the five operators reading them, four metrics, three thresholds, two prompt variants and five seeds: 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 pre-registered specifications.
errors.evidence: 'The grid contains seven objectives, seven operators, four corruption distributions nested within the five operators reading them, four metrics, three thresholds, two prompt variants and five seeds: 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 pre-registered specifications.' and 'Two operators never read corruption; crossing them with corruption would duplicate specifications.' Using the paper's own breakdown: operator-corruption combinations = 5*4 + 2*1 = 22; discovery cells expected = 7 objectives * 22 * 4 metrics = 616. Then specs = 616 * 3 thresholds * 2 prompts * 5 seeds = 18,480. Therefore the listed grid factors imply 616 discovery cells (and 18,480 specs), so the paper's claim of '1,540 discovery cells' contradicts its stated grid decomposition.
errors.explanation: The paper's factor list (7 objectives × (5*4 + 2*1) operator-corruption combos × 4 metrics) yields 616 discovery cells; the reported 18,480 specs matches 616 × 3 × 2 × 5, so '1,540 discovery cells' is inconsistent with the same paragraph's factorization.

errors.claim: Failed objective cells 220 (and Realised discovery cells 1,320).
errors.evidence: 'One objective fails throughout its arm: “Grid consequence” table, “Failed objective cells” 220 and “Realised objectives” 6' and 'Realised discovery cells 1,320.' But using the paper's stated grid decomposition (see evidence above) total discovery cells should be 616, so discovery-cells per objective = 616 / 7 = 88, not 220. The 220 failed cells figure therefore contradicts the paper's own grid-factor accounting.
errors.explanation: If the grid factors in the same section are used, each objective covers 88 discovery cells; claiming 220 failed cells for one objective is inconsistent with that accounting.

errors.claim: "Observed/chance overlap | about 45 times"
errors.evidence: Structural diagnostic table rows: "Median shared-edge fraction | 4%" and "Random line at median size | 0.0031" (also Table 3 J6D: mean Jaccard reported as 0.1396).
errors.explanation: The table's median Jaccard is 4% (0.04); using the stated random-line value 0.0031 gives 0.04 / 0.0031 ≈ 12.9, not ≈45. A factor of ≈45 would follow from using the mean Jaccard 0.1396 (0.1396 / 0.0031 ≈ 45.0). The table therefore mixes median and mean statistics when reporting the 'observed/chance overlap' factor, which is internally inconsistent.

errors.claim: "Instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges."
errors.evidence: "Thus 2,692 of 7,561 specifications contribute no flips; instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges." (paragraph)" and Table 7 row: "2,000 | 312 | 0.5714 | 3 | 0.0000 | 1"
errors.explanation: The claim that all instability is below 2,000 edges contradicts the table row for size 2,000, which shows discovered F = 0.5714 and 3 classes (i.e. flips) at 2,000 edges, so instability is present at 2,000 edges.

errors.claim: "Its degeneracy occurs above 1,000 edges."
errors.evidence: "A6N samples the full edge population with R=1,000 null multiverses... Its degeneracy occurs above 1,000 edges." (opening sentence)" and later: "A6N collapses at and above 1,000 edges; discovery also collapses at 5,000 and 10,000." plus Table 7 row: "1,000 | 380 | 0.5133 | 3 | 0.0000 | 1"

final_notes: Key reported results: pooled instability F = 0.7316 (95% CI 0.7247–0.7380); mean Jaccard = 0.1396; pooled functional gap F - (1 - agreement) = 0.3344. Circuits retained: 7,561 (by size: 10:2492, 20:489, 50:519, 100:242, 200:199, 500:236, 1,000:380, 2,000:312, 5,000:625, 10,000:2067). Discovered-F by size: 10:0.4543, 20:0.3380, 50:0.4639, 100:0.5792, 200:0.5122, 500:0.4258, 1,000:0.5133, 2,000:0.5714, 5,000:0.0000, 10,000:0.0000 (discovery collapse at 5k+10k). A6N null F collapses to 0.0000 at 1,000+. Functional diagnostics (§7.6): pooled per-example agreement 0.6028 (instability 0.3972), smallest-circuit instability 0.4777, Cohen's kappa 0.0146 (within-size 0.016–0.047), raw agreement 0.52–0.92, accuracy 0.51–0.95; pooled-gap band carries 500–2,000 edges. Y3W protocol: declare S and code φ, compute π* and F, pass if π* ≥ 1−α, report π*, F, discard rates and within-group decompositions. Limitations: single-model study; planned second model (M9B/Pythia-160m) unrun (924-cell grid). Size is an outcome and materially alters conclusions (fixed-size F ≈ 0.2706 vs smallest residual ≈ 0.5939); Table 6 best residual F = 0.5939 (95% CI 0.5803–0.6063). Grid consequences: 220 failed objective cells, 8,279 specs admitting no circuit, 52.3% discard rate. Bootstrapping caveat: one family invalid; unusable intervals replaced by point estimates; no bias-corrected estimator used. Reproducibility (new): public timestamped commit tagged 'prereg-p1-confirmatory'; archive verification establishes one environment across all 1,320 confirmatory cells; content-addressed archive vs git: 22/22 files identical; analysis needs no GPU. One script recomputes headline quantities: 36 checks, 0 failures (F checked via three routes incl. brute-force pairs); another checks every manuscript numeric token against stored-result derivations; tables emitted directly; test suite contains 343 tests.

Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Pre-registered crossed design for GPT-2 small (Q7V) on indirect-object identification (Z4K); committed but unrun second-model plan: Pythia-160m (M9B). Deterministic code G7U maps discovered circuits to structured Annex IV statements; 7,561 claim-producing specifications; pairwise claim disagreement F = 0.7316 (pooled). Removing size from statements and conditioning on size reduces disagreement to 0.2706. Discovered circuits outperform size-matched random null (A6N) at fixed size; pooled comparison reverses. Graph: factorised (query/key/value) with |E| = 32,491 edges; 12 blocks, 12 heads/block (144 heads), 12 MLPs. Specification s = (objective o, ablation operator a, corruption distribution d, metric m, size threshold τ, prompt variant P, seed r, granularity g). Ablation operators: 7 total (five read corruption, two do not); d nested within operators that read corruption. Granularities: COARSE (E7R), MEDIUM (K8Z), FINE (V2H). Metrics (four): comprehensiveness (T9V), KL divergence (H2W), logit difference (N6C), sufficiency (U4J). Discovery: crossed grid, discovery cell counted before metric/threshold/statement reporting; metric-relative threshold rule; retention/discard rates tracked; one objective arm failed (MSE/integral target runtime error). Statistical tooling: Jaccard α = intersection/union, α-bar = mean over unordered pairs; D = 1 - Jaccard; F defined in Gini–Simpson form (pair disagreement); G and F_within(G) for conditioning; pi* = max_class_share; Y3W filability requires pi* >= 1 - alpha (alpha = filing tolerance). Nulls: R = 1,000 null multiverses; null degeneracy = collapse. Inference: bootstrap B = 10,000 resamples of specifications; pairwise U-statistics for F and α-bar; p-values not reported (grid not independent). Functional diagnostics: agreement, functional instability = 1 - agreement, functional gap = F - (1 - agreement), Cohen's kappa, accuracy. Structural variance: REML over log10(size). Discovery families: edge-attribution patching (R8X), integrated edge gradients (B3Q); optimal ablation (C4Y) unsupported. Pre-registration artifacts: deviations file, six-cell validation slice, environment fingerprint, content-addressed git tree, tag 'prereg-p1-confirmatory'. GPU not required.

errors.claim: "Note the ceiling: F\leq 1-1/k for k claim classes, so a reported flip rate must be read against the number of classes the map can produce. With the nine classes observed here the ceiling is 0.8889, and the observed 0.7316 is 82.3% of it. F is not near one by construction."
errors.evidence: "Equation 2: F = 1 - \frac{\sum_{c} n_{c}(n_{c}-1)}{N(N-1)}" (the finite-sample Gini–Simpson form) and the quoted ceiling sentence above.
errors.explanation: The displayed formula for F is the without-replacement (finite-sample) form; in fact F = (N/(N-1))*(1 - \sum_c p_c^2). The maximum over distributions p_c (uniform p_c=1/k) gives F_max = (N/(N-1))*(1 - 1/k), which can exceed 1 - 1/k for finite N (and equals 1 when N=k and each class has n_c=1). Thus the statement "F \le 1-1/k" is mathematically incorrect for the estimator in Eq.2.

errors.claim: "Note the ceiling: F\leq 1-1/k for k claim classes, so a reported flip rate must be read against the number of classes the map can produce. With the nine classes observed here the ceiling is 0.8889, and the observed 0.7316 is 82.3% of it. F is not near one by construction."
errors.evidence: "Equation 2: F = 1 - \frac{\sum_{c} n_{c}(n_{c}-1)}{N(N-1)}" (the finite-sample Gini–Simpson form) and the quoted ceiling sentence above.
errors.explanation: The displayed formula for F is the without-replacement (finite-sample) form; in fact F = (N/(N-1))*(1 - \sum_c p_c^2). The maximum over distributions p_c (uniform p_c=1/k) gives F_max = (N/(N-1))*(1 - 1/k), which can exceed 1 - 1/k for finite N (and equals 1 when N=k and each class has n_c=1). Thus the statement "F \le 1-1/k" is mathematically incorrect for the estimator in Eq.2.

Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability. Author: Ajay Pravin Mahale. Date: 12 Aug 2026. Domain: circuit-level interpretability. Main claim (from preface): circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across plausibly acceptable tolerances: competent analysts using the same system and tool can produce incompatible statements under different defensible settings. Limitation: applicability beyond the single model/task studied remains untested. Introduction notes: auditing framed as requiring two auditors to reach the same conclusion (a commissioning requirement, not an ML definition). Regulatory motivation: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (consolidated text amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, CELEX 02024R1689-20260727; read 11 Aug 2026) asks for “general logic” (Annex IV 2(b)) and measures to facilitate interpretation (2(e)); Article 86(1) asks for clear explanations of the AI system’s role. Mechanistic interpretability (circuit discovery) returns a subgraph said to explain behavior; filing such accounts presumes compatibility between analysts. Study design: pre-registered crossed design using published implementations only; circuits are converted into structured Annex IV statements deterministically. Controls standardize individual axes, remove claim-size dependence, and condition on size. Key reported empirical result: three pooled statistics invert when selected objects differ in size. Paper does not propose improved discovery methods—the objection targets the standard assumed when filing current evidence; uses a standards-body decision rule to measure regulatory-claim movement across defensible specifications.

Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability. Author/date: Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026. Domain: circuit-level (mechanistic) interpretability; regulatory filing focus. Main claim: circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across plausibly acceptable tolerances—competent analysts using the same system and tool can produce incompatible statements under different defensible settings. Limitation: single model/task only; broader applicability untested. Study design: pre-registered crossed design using published implementations only; circuits converted deterministically into structured Annex IV statements. Controls standardize individual axes, remove claim-size dependence, condition on size. Key empirical result noted earlier: three pooled statistics invert when selected objects differ in size. Related work (this part): Non-identifiability (Méloux et al. [6]) — behaviours need not have unique mechanistic explanations; paper focuses downstream cost for filing. Faithfulness metric sensitivity (Miller et al. [8]) — ablation-based faithfulness sensitive to researcher choices; a single-axis sensitivity of Miller et al. is extended here into a seven-axis regulatory propagation; Miller’s released library used as instrument (under its definitions). Structure vs function (Bayat Makou et al. [1]) — structurally distinct circuits can implement same computation (W5T: phantom specialisation); motivates using functional measurement to address equivalence-class objections. Variance as estimation (Méloux et al. [7]) — interpretability viewed as estimation with estimator/seed variance; seed variance included as an axis. Auditability (Lan et al. [4], Sharkey et al. [10], Mueller et al. [9]) — prior conflicting conclusions motivate measurement/criteria and need for standardised evaluation/specification for certification. Multiverse method (Steegen et al. [13]; Simonsohn et al. [12] F9A specification curve; Simmons et al. [11]) — adopt multiverse/specification-curve techniques to expose analytic flexibility. Explanation metrics under optimisation pressure (Hsia et al. [3]) — U4J and T9V can be inflated without changing predictions/explanations; both are among the paper’s four metrics; metric-specific discard reporting used to avoid silent pooling.

final_notes: Paper: circuit-level interpretability on GPT-2 small (Q7V), task Z4K. Preregistered grid 18,480 specs; realized 15,840; claim-producing specs 7,561; pooled Discovered F = 0.7316 (pooled Discovered vs A6N comparisons reported). Section 7.1: distinct circuits 3,218; median D = 0.960; median circuit size 200 edges. Axis-standardised residual F by factor: evaluation metric 0.5939 (95% CI 0.5803–0.6063) up to Seed 0.7307. REML variance decomposition: Ablation–corruption interaction 78.8%, Residual 11.5%, Ablation 4.4%, Threshold 4.1%, Metric 0.7%. Metric-standardised percentage disagreement 49.4%. Fixed-size dominant-layer F = 0.2706 (95% CI 0.2550–0.2859). Table 7 size-sum n=7,561; text claims degeneracy ‘above 1,000’ but table thresholds differ. 2,692 specs produced no flips; instability concentrated below ≈2,000 edges. Functional diagnostics: pooled agreement 0.6028; functional instability 0.3972; smallest-circuit instability 0.4777; Cohen’s kappa reported 0.0146 while per-size kappa range given as 0.016–0.047 (inconsistent). Raw agreement climbs 0.52→0.92; accuracy 0.51→0.95; pooled gap band ~500–2,000 edges. Y3W protocol: declare S and φ, compute π* and F, pass if π* ≥ 1−α, report π*, F, discard rates, within-group decompositions; filings that cannot state π* treated as asserted. Limitations: one model/one task; committed second-model plan M9B (Pythia-160m) reported as a 924-cell grid with inconsistent seed-level counts vs earlier description; circuit size treated as outcome not axis; multiverse limited by library (C4Y optimal ablation excluded); discard rate high/uneven; bootstrap invalid for conditioning groups of 2–5 specs; no bias-corrected estimator after naive intervals disagreed. Reproducibility (this part): public timestamped commit tagged 'prereg-p1-confirmatory'; archive verification establishes one environment across all 1,320 confirmatory cells; content-addressed comparison recovers code commit 22 of 22 files identical; analysis needs no GPU. One script recomputes headline quantities: 36 checks, 0 failures, F computed via three routes including brute-force pairs. Another script checks every manuscript numeric token against stored-result derivations; tables emitted directly, never transcribed; full test suite contains 343 tests.

Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability. Author: Ajay Pravin Mahale. Date: 12 Aug 2026. Domain: circuit-level interpretability. Main claim (from preface): circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across plausibly acceptable tolerances: competent analysts using the same system and tool can produce incompatible statements under different defensible settings. Faithfulness metric sensitivity (Miller et al. Structure vs function (Bayat Makou et al. [13]; Simonsohn et al. [12] F9A specification curve; Simmons et al. [11]) — adopt multiverse/specification-curve techniques to expose analytic flexibility. Explanation metrics under optimisation pressure (Hsia et al. [3]) — U4J and T9V can be inflated without changing predictions/explanations; both are among the paper’s four metrics; metric-specific discard reporting used to avoid silent pooling.

steps.notes_before: Model: GPT-2 small, indirect object ID. Pre-registered: claimed 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 specifications; one objective failed entirely (220 cells), yielding realised grid 1,320 cells and 15,840 specs. Metric-relative threshold discarded 8,279 of 15,840 specs (52.3%), leaving 7,561 kept specs. Kept-by-metric counts: comprehensiveness 3,947; KL 1,467; logit-diff 1,270; sufficiency 877. Jaccard mean \bar J = 0.1396 (95% CI 0.1377–0.1418), computed exactly over choose(7,561,2)=28,580,580 specification pairs; 7,561 specs correspond to 3,218 distinct circuits. Pairwise D quantiles (1%,25%,50%,75%) = (0.196, 0.788, 0.960, 0.998) → median J ≈ 4%. At median circuit size k=200 the analytic random expectation is 0.0031. Paper states observed overlap ≈45× chance (in Section 7.1) — but comparing median J to 0.0031 gives ≈13×; 45× fits mean-based comparison (0.1396/0.0031≈45), so the wording/compare-basis is inconsistent. Flip rate F = 0.7316 (95% CI 0.7247–0.7380); modal share π* = 0.4109; Table 4 counts sum to 7,561. Coarse aggregation: early 47.9%, late 43.6%, middle 8.5%. All six addressee×granularity combos reject filability per text.

errors.claim: Cohen’s kappa is 0.0146.

final_notes: Key outcomes: pooled discovered claim-instability F = 0.7316 [0.7247, 0.7380]; mean J̄ = 0.1396 [0.1377, 0.1418]; claim-flip pair disagreement ≈73.2% (CI 0.725–0.738). Modal claim classes early/distributed 0.4109, late/sparse 0.2848; aggregated early/late/middle 47.9%/43.6%/8.5%. Table 6 (single-axis residuals): best residual F = 0.5939 (59.4%); other residuals — Ablation 0.7014; Discovery objective 0.7018; Threshold 0.7070; Corruption 0.7092; Prompt 0.7232; Seed 0.7307. REML log10 contributions: ablation×corruption 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric 0.7%. Size conditioning largest effect: size-free fixed-size F = 0.2706 (CI 0.2550–0.2859); conditioning on size reduces F far more than any single-axis standardisation. Null/comparison: pooled discovered 0.7316 vs A6N 0.6774; fixed-size K8Z discovered 0.2746 vs A6N 0.4230; fixed-size E7R discovered 0.2706 vs A6N 0.3822. Many within-size rows had no flips (e.g., 5k+10k = 2,692 of 7,561 specs). Diagnostics: pooled agreement 0.6028 (instability 0.3972); smallest-circuit instability 0.4777; pooled Cohen’s κ 0.0146; raw agreement 0.52–0.92; sizes failing gap threshold 6/10; pooled-gap band 500–2,000 edges. Y3W protocol: declare S and φ, compute π* = max_c n_c/N, report F; pass if π* ≥ 1−α; report π*, F, discard rates, within-group decompositions. Limitations: single model/task; planned but unrun second model; circuit size treated as outcome not axis; discards high/uneven (grid consequence 52.3% — 220 failed objective cells, 8,279 specs with no circuit); bootstrap invalid for one family. Reproducibility: public commit tagged "prereg-p1-confirmatory"; every reported number traces to configuration, seed and environment fingerprint; archive verification across all 1,320 confirmatory cells; content-addressed comparison recovered code: 22/22 files identical; analysis needs no GPU. One script recomputes headline quantities: 36 checks, 0 failures, F checked via three routes incl. brute-force pairs; another checks every manuscript numeric token vs stored-result derivations; tables emitted directly; full test suite contains 343 tests.

Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Pre-registered crossed design using published implementations to discover circuits for GPT-2 small on indirect object identification. Deterministic code converts discovered circuits into structured Annex IV statements. 7,561 claim-producing specifications; pairwise claim disagreement = 0.7316. "No single-axis standardisation permits filing under the registered tolerances." Removing size from statements and conditioning comparisons on size reduces disagreement to 0.2706. Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Pre-registered crossed design for GPT-2 small (Q7V) on indirect-object identification (Z4K); committed but unrun second-model plan: Pythia-160m (M9B). Deterministic code G7U maps discovered circuits to structured Annex IV statements; 7,561 claim-producing specifications; pairwise claim disagreement F = 0.7316 (pooled). Removing size from statements and conditioning on size reduces disagreement to 0.2706. Discovered circuits outperform size-matched random null (A6N) at fixed size; pooled comparison reverses. Graph: factorised (query/key/value) with |E| = 32,491 edges; 12 blocks, 12 heads/block (144 heads), 12 MLPs. Specification s = (objective o, ablation operator a, corruption distribution d, metric m, size threshold τ, prompt variant P, seed r, granularity g). Ablation operators: 7 total (five read corruption, two do not); d nested within operators that read corruption. Granularities: COARSE (E7R), MEDIUM (K8Z), FINE (V2H). Metrics (four): comprehensiveness (T9V), KL divergence (H2W), logit difference (N6C), sufficiency (U4J). Discovery: crossed grid, discovery cell counted before metric/threshold/statement reporting; metric-relative threshold rule; retention/discard rates tracked; one objective arm failed (MSE/integral target runtime error). Statistical tooling: Jaccard α = intersection/union, α-bar = mean over unordered pairs; D = 1 - Jaccard; F defined in Gini–Simpson form (pair disagreement); G and F_within(G) for conditioning; pi* = max_class_share; Y3W filability requires pi* >= 1 - alpha (alpha = filing tolerance). Nulls: R = 1,000 null multiverses; null degeneracy = collapse. Inference: bootstrap B = 10,000 resamples of specifications; pairwise U-statistics for F and α-bar; p-values not reported (grid not independent). Functional diagnostics: agreement, functional instability = 1 - agreement, functional gap = F - (1 - agreement), Cohen's kappa, accuracy. Structural variance: REML over log10(size). Discovery families: edge-attribution patching (R8X), integrated edge gradients (B3Q); optimal ablation (C4Y) unsupported. Pre-registration artifacts: deviations file, six-cell validation slice, environment fingerprint, content-addressed git tree, tag 'prereg-p1-confirmatory'. GPU not required.

Specification tuple s = (objective o, ablation operator a, corruption distribution d, metric m, size threshold τ, prompt variant P, seed r, granularity g) — note possible axis-count ambiguity (tuple lists 8 elements but related work claims seven axes). Ablation operators: 7 total (five read-corruption, two not); corruption d nested within read-corruption operators. Granularity levels: COARSE, MEDIUM, FINE. Metrics: comprehensiveness, KL divergence, logit difference, sufficiency (paper maps sufficiency=U4J and comprehensiveness=T9V in related work). Nulls: R = 1,000 null multiverses; null degeneracy = collapse. Inference: bootstrap B = 10,000 resamples; pairwise U-statistics for F and ᾱ. Related work cited: non-identifiability (Méloux), faithfulness sensitivity (Miller), structure vs function (Bayat Makou), variance-as-estimation (Méloux seed variance), auditability (Lan et al.), multiverse/specification-curve methods (Steegen/Simonsohn), and metrics-inflation examples (Hsia).

steps.notes_before: Paper: Explanation Multiplicity (pre-registered). Model: GPT-2 small (Q7V). Specification tuple s = (o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g) — eight axes (axis-count ambiguity noted). Claim map G7U maps discovery output C(s) ⊆ E to structured Annex IV statements. Edge set size |E| = 32,491. Components: 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 total; text also says output receives 157 non-terminal sources (inconsistency flagged). For block index b, attention receives 1+13b sources at three input slots per each of 12 heads. Circuit instability D(s_i,s_j) = 1 - Jaccard(C_i,C_j); ̅J is mean Jaccard over unordered pairs. Claim instability F = 1 - Σ_c n_c(n_c-1) / [N(N-1)] (Gini–Simpson); within-group F_within(G) formula given. Ceiling: F ≤ 1 - 1/k; observed classes k=9 → ceiling 0.8889; observed fraction of ceiling 82.3% → observed F ≈ 0.731. Total claim-producing specifications: 7,561. Ablation operators: 7 levels (read-corruption nested); granularity: COARSE/MEDIUM/FINE. Null multiverses R=1,000; bootstrap B=10,000. Structural diagnostic: median D = 0.960. Functional diagnostic: Cohen's kappa = 0.0146. Earlier note: authors claim discovered circuits outperform size-matched random null A6N, but cited numbers in Sec.7.5 (0.2746 vs 0.4230; 0.2706 vs 0.3822) appear inconsistent with that claim.

Section G7U defines the claim mapping and reports sensitivity of F to size-binning choices. Size bins follow a committed calibration on a measured node-count curve (not tuned to F). Table 1 values: committed bins F=0.7316; all thresholds ×0.5: 0.7448; ×0.8: 0.7435; ×0.9: 0.7394; ×1.1: 0.7289; ×1.25: 0.7314; ×1.5: 0.7308; ×2: 0.7232; equal thirds: 0.7018; deciles: 0.7719; no size term (E7R): 0.5733. Sensitivity range across factor-four binnings reported as 0.70–0.77. Claim: four alternatives exceed the committed result (×0.5, ×0.8, ×0.9, deciles). Regulatory addressee mappings: D9P (overseer) orders layer band (early/middle/late), size class (sparse/moderate/distributed), ranked input segment; L3X (affected) leads with input segment. Resolutions: E7R=COARSE (coarsest), K8Z=MEDIUM, V2H=FINE; nested so refinements cannot contradict coarser statements. Claim map φ is pre-registered deterministic code. Carry-forward key earlier numbers and flags: specification tuple s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g) (axis-count ambiguity noted); claim map G7U; |E|=32,491; components: 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs (156) (earlier noted inconsistency with a 157 count flagged); total claim-producing specs 7,561; nulls R=1,000, bootstrap B=10,000; ceiling F≤1-1/k with k=9 → ceiling≈0.8889 and observed F≈0.731; structural diagnostic median D=0.960; functional diagnostic Cohen’s κ=0.0146. Previously flagged potential inconsistency: authors' claim circuits outperform size-matched random null A6N (Sec.7.5 numbers looked inconsistent).

Section 6 (Method): Grid axes — 7 objectives; 7 operators (5 operators read 4 corruption distributions each; 2 operators ignore corruption) ; 4 metrics (T9V, H2W (KL), N6C (logit diff), U4J); 3 thresholds; 2 prompt variants; 5 seeds. Operator×corruption combos = 5*4 + 2 = 22. Reported counts: discovery cells = 1,540; pre-registered specifications = 18,480 (consistent with 7*22*4*3*2*5 = 18,480 when corruption nesting is applied). Discovery cell appears to index objectives × operator-corruption × prompts × seeds (7*22*2*5 = 1,540); pre-registered specs = discovery cells × 4 metrics × 3 thresholds = 18,480. Methods used: R8X (edge-attribution patching) and B3Q (integrated edge gradients); lineage and corruption sources cited. Pre-registration: plan and directional abstracts committed; append-only deviations file recorded. Statistics: no specification-level p-values; nonparametric bootstrap resamples specifications (B = 10,000); F and J̄ are pairwise U-statistics; CIs condition on the grid. Exclusions: one objective fails fully — "Failed objective cells" = 220 → realised objectives = 6; realised discovery cells = 1,320; realised specifications = 15,840. Specifications admitting no circuit = 8,279 → claim-producing (admitting circuits) = 7,561; overall discard rate = 52.3%. Metric-specific retention (kept / discarded / discard rate): T9V 3,947 / 13 / 0.003; H2W 1,467 / 2,493 / 0.630; N6C 1,270 / 2,690 / 0.679; U4J 877 / 3,083 / 0.779. Designed T9V composition 25% → surviving T9V composition 52%. Carry-forward from earlier: spec tuple s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g) (axis-count ambiguity noted); claim map G7U pre-registered; |E|=32,491; components 144 heads + 12 MLPs = 156 (earlier flagged 157 inconsistency); nulls R=1,000; bootstrap B=10,000; ceiling ≤1-1/k (k=9) ≈0.8889; observed F ≈0.731; structural diagnostic median D = 0.960; functional diagnostic Cohen's κ = 0.0146.

errors.claim: "Note the ceiling: F\leq 1-1/k for k claim classes, so a reported flip rate must be read against the number of classes the map can produce. With the nine classes observed here the ceiling is 0.8889, and the observed 0.7316 is 82.3% of it. F is not near one by construction."
errors.evidence: "Equation 2: F = 1 - \frac{\sum_{c} n_{c}(n_{c}-1)}{N(N-1)}" (the finite-sample Gini–Simpson form) and the quoted ceiling sentence above.
errors.explanation: The displayed formula for F is the without-replacement (finite-sample) form; in fact F = (N/(N-1))*(1 - \sum_c p_c^2). The maximum over distributions p_c (uniform p_c=1/k) gives F_max = (N/(N-1))*(1 - 1/k), which can exceed 1 - 1/k for finite N (and equals 1 when N=k and each class has n_c=1). Thus the statement "F \le 1-1/k" is mathematically incorrect for the estimator in Eq.2.

errors.claim: "The median pair of circuits shares 4% of its edges, and only 1% of pairs exceed a Jaccard of 0.8. At the median circuit size of 200 edges the analytic random line k/(2|E|-k) gives 0.0031, so observed overlap is about 45 times chance."

Paper: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Research question: whether mechanistic/circuit discovery evidence is robust to defensible analytic variation (two competent analysts, same system and tool, different defensible settings). Method: pre-registered crossed grid of 7 analytic axes (levels taken from published implementations); mapped each discovered circuit via a deterministic claim map to a structured Annex IV statement. Dataset/experiment: GPT-2 small on an indirect object identification task; 15,840 pre-registered specifications, of which 7,561 produced a claim. Main results: derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs (95% CI 0.725–0.738); modal claim covers 41.1% of the space. Standardising the most influential axis (evaluation metric) yields flip rate 59.4%. Removing circuit size from the claim and holding it fixed yields flip rate 27.1% (95% CI 0.255–0.286), still above the pre-registered threshold (threshold value not given here). Circuits are near-disjoint (median pairwise Jaccard overlap 4%) and functionally uncorrelated (Cohen's kappa 0.015) — authors argue instability is not merely one mechanism restated. They provide a filability criterion/protocol and report one of seven documented discovery objectives fails to execute on the library's canonical task. Study limitation: single model and single task; generalisability untested.

errors.claim: "Note the ceiling: F\leq 1-1/k for k claim classes, so a reported flip rate must be read against the number of classes the map can produce. With the nine classes observed here the ceiling is 0.8889, and the observed 0.7316 is 82.3% of it. F is not near one by construction."
errors.evidence: "Equation 2: F = 1 - \frac{\sum_{c} n_{c}(n_{c}-1)}{N(N-1)}" (the finite-sample Gini–Simpson form) and the quoted ceiling sentence above.
errors.explanation: The displayed formula for F is the without-replacement (finite-sample) form; in fact F = (N/(N-1))*(1 - \sum_c p_c^2). The maximum over distributions p_c (uniform p_c=1/k) gives F_max = (N/(N-1))*(1 - 1/k), which can exceed 1 - 1/k for finite N (and equals 1 when N=k and each class has n_c=1). Thus the statement "F \le 1-1/k" is mathematically incorrect for the estimator in Eq.2.

Model/task: GPT-2 small on indirect-object identification. Methods: edge-attribution patching family + integrated edge gradients (library from Miller et al.); automated circuit discovery lineage Conmy et al.; four corruption levels from Wang et al. Grid (pre-registered): 7 discovery objectives, 7 ablation operators (5 of which read 4 corruption distributions; 2 never read corruption), 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompt variants, 5 seeds. Grid: 7,561 claim-producing specifications → 3,218 distinct circuits. Pairwise D quantiles: 1% 0.196, 25% 0.788, median 0.960, 75% 0.998. Median circuit size 200 edges; median shared-edge fraction 4%; analytic random Jaccard at median size 0.0031; expected random overlap for 500-edge circuits 0.008. Pooled discovered F = 0.7316 (CI 0.7247–0.7380). Axis-standardised residuals: metric F 0.5939 (removes 0.1377); seed 0.7307 (removes 0.0009). REML: ablation–corruption interaction explains 78.8% of structural variance; metric-standardised percentage disagreement 59.4%. Fixed-size pooled F = 0.2706 (95% CI 0.2550–0.2859; reported 27.1%). Pooled vs A6N: 0.7316 vs 0.6774. Fixed-size rows: K8Z discovered 0.2746 vs A6N 0.4230; E7R discovered 0.2706 vs A6N 0.3822. A6N degeneracy above 1,000 edges; discovery collapses at 5,000 and 10,000 edges (Table 7), leaving 2,692 specs with no flips. Y3W protocol: declare S and φ, compute π* = max_c n_c/N over S and F, evidence passes at tolerance α iff π* ≥ 1−α, report π*, F, discard rates per axis level, within-group decompositions. Limitations: one model/task; planned second-model M9B (Pythia-160m) 924-cell grid unrun; instrument library excludes C4Y (optimal ablation) so measured F is a lower bound; discard rate high/uneven; bootstrap invalid for some small conditioning groups (2–5 specs); unusable intervals replaced by point estimates. Reproducibility (part 11): public commit tag 'prereg-p1-confirmatory'; archive verification finds one environment across all 1,540 confirmatory cells; content-addressed comparison recovers code commit, 22/22 files identical; analysis needs no GPU. One script recomputes headline quantities: 36 checks, 0 failures, F via three routes including brute-force pairs. Another script checks every manuscript numeric token; tables emitted directly; test suite contains 343 tests.

Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability. Author: Ajay Pravin Mahale. Date: 12 Aug 2026. Domain: circuit-level interpretability. Regulatory motivation: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (consolidated text amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, CELEX 02024R1689-20260727; read 11 Aug 2026) asks for “general logic” (Annex IV 2(b)) and measures to facilitate interpretation (2(e)); Article 86(1) asks for clear explanations of the AI system’s role. errors.claim: "Note the ceiling: F\leq 1-1/k for k claim classes, so a reported flip rate must be read against the number of classes the map can produce. With the nine classes observed here the ceiling is 0.8889, and the observed 0.7316 is 82.3% of it. F is not near one by construction."
errors.evidence: "Equation 2: F = 1 - \frac{\sum_{c} n_{c}(n_{c}-1)}{N(N-1)}" (the finite-sample Gini–Simpson form) and the quoted ceiling sentence above.
errors.explanation: The displayed formula for F is the without-replacement (finite-sample) form; in fact F = (N/(N-1))*(1 - \sum_c p_c^2). The maximum over distributions p_c (uniform p_c=1/k) gives F_max = (N/(N-1))*(1 - 1/k), which can exceed 1 - 1/k for finite N (and equals 1 when N=k and each class has n_c=1). Thus the statement "F \le 1-1/k" is mathematically incorrect for the estimator in Eq.2.

Paper: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Research question: whether mechanistic/circuit discovery evidence is robust to defensible analytic variation (two competent analysts, same system and tool, different defensible settings). Method: pre-registered crossed grid of 7 analytic axes (levels taken from published implementations); mapped each discovered circuit via a deterministic claim map to a structured Annex IV statement. Main results: derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs (95% CI 0.725–0.738); modal claim covers 41.1% of the space. Standardising the most influential axis (evaluation metric) yields flip rate 59.4%. Removing circuit size from the claim and holding it fixed yields flip rate 27.1% (95% CI 0.255–0.286), still above the pre-registered threshold (threshold value not given here). Study limitation: single model and single task; generalisability untested.

errors.claim: "Note the ceiling: F\leq 1-1/k for k claim classes, so a reported flip rate must be read against the number of classes the map can produce. With the nine classes observed here the ceiling is 0.8889, and the observed 0.7316 is 82.3% of it. F is not near one by construction."
errors.evidence: "Equation 2: F = 1 - \frac{\sum_{c} n_{c}(n_{c}-1)}{N(N-1)}" (the finite-sample Gini–Simpson form) and the quoted ceiling sentence above.
errors.explanation: The displayed formula for F is the without-replacement (finite-sample) form; in fact F = (N/(N-1))*(1 - \sum_c p_c^2). The maximum over distributions p_c (uniform p_c=1/k) gives F_max = (N/(N-1))*(1 - 1/k), which can exceed 1 - 1/k for finite N (and equals 1 when N=k and each class has n_c=1). Thus the statement "F \le 1-1/k" is mathematically incorrect for the estimator in Eq.2.

Model/task: GPT-2 small on indirect-object identification. Methods: edge-attribution patching family + integrated edge gradients (library from Miller et al.); automated circuit discovery lineage Conmy et al.; four corruption levels from Wang et al. Grid (pre-registered): 7 discovery objectives, 7 ablation operators (5 of which read 4 corruption distributions; 2 never read corruption), 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompt variants, 5 seeds. This yields 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 specifications pre-registered (cells include prompt×seed; specs per cell = metrics×thresholds = 12). Two pre-specified exclusions applied before any circuit was seen: one entire discovery objective failed at runtime (all 220 of its cells), so the realised grid = 6 objectives, 1,320 cells and 15,840 specifications. The metric-relative threshold rule produced no circuit for 8,279 of the 15,840 specifications (discard rate 52.3%), leaving 7,561 surviving specs/claims. Table 2 (discard by metric): comprehensiveness kept 3,947 / discarded 13 (discard rate 0.003); KL divergence kept 1,467 / discarded 2,493 (0.630); logit difference kept 1,270 / discarded 2,690 (0.679); sufficiency kept 877 / discarded 3,083 (0.779). Surviving-pool composition: comprehensiveness = 3,947/7,561 ≈ 52% (vs 25% by design). Statistics: no p-values; uncertainty via nonparametric bootstrap resampling specifications (not pairs) B=10,000 because F and J̄ are U-statistics; intervals conditional on the grid. Keep earlier definitions/results: φ pre-registered deterministic claim map; 15,840 specs, 7,561 produced a claim; observed F ≈ 0.7316, modal share ≈ 41.1%; |E|=32,491 for GPT-2 small; circuit instability Jaccard-based D(s_i,s_j).

Filability protocol: spec space S, deterministic claim map φ, π* = max_c n_c/N; filable if π* ≥ 1−α; report π*, F, discard rates, within-group decompositions. Limitations: one model/task; planned Pythia replication unrun; circuit size is outcome of threshold and distorts pooled stats; instrument omits optimal ablation (F is a lower bound); retained pool metric-imbalanced; bootstrap invalid for groups of 2–5. Pooled discovered flip F = 0.7316 vs pooled null F = 0.6774 (R=1,000 random multiverses from 32,491 edges); H3 rejected because distributions separated with disjoint intervals, but the pooled direction is attributed to circuit-size confounding — holding size fixed reverses the ordering (medium: discovered ≈0.2746 vs null 0.4230; coarse: 0.2706 vs 0.3822). Table 7: null predictions collapse to one class at ≥1,000 edges (null F = 0.0000); discovered predictions collapse at 5,000 and 10,000 edges (n=625 and 2,067; F = 0.0000), so 2,692 specs produce no flips. H4 (pooled): per-example functional agreement ≈0.6028 → instability ≈0.3972; gap to claim flip = 0.3344 (95% CI [0.3297, 0.3394]) > 0.10, so H4 supported at pooled level but qualified by failures at 6 of 10 sizes and negative gaps at 5 sizes; pooled H4 signal mainly driven by the 500–2,000 edge band. Agreement/accuracy metrics: raw agreement ≈0.60 (size-specific 0.52–0.92); accuracy range 0.51–0.95. Note: paper reports overall Cohen's kappa 0.0146 but also per-size kappas 0.016–0.047 (previously flagged inconsistency). New (Part 14): Filability protocol requires a declared specification space S, a deterministic claim map φ (published code, not a language model), and measured agreement. Compute π* = max_c n_c/N over S and compute flip rate F (Eq.2). A claim is filable at tolerance α if π* ≥ 1 − α. Filers must report π*, F, discard rate by axis level, and within-group decomposition of any pooled statistic. Claim that "coarse overseer filings are more stable than coarse affected-person filings" and that the regulator need not adjudicate which analytic choice is correct.

final_notes: Key results: pooled discovered F = 0.7316 (vs A6N 0.6774). Fixed-size discovered: K8Z 0.2746 (A6N 0.4230); E7R 0.2706 (A6N 0.3822). Ablation operators: 7 total (five read corruption, two do not); d nested within operators that read corruption. Granularities: COARSE (E7R), MEDIUM (K8Z), FINE (V2H). Statistical tooling: Jaccard α = intersection/union, α-bar = mean over unordered pairs; D = 1 - Jaccard; F defined in Gini–Simpson form (pair disagreement); G and F_within(G) for conditioning; pi* = max_class_share; Y3W filability requires pi* >= 1 - alpha (alpha = filing tolerance). Nulls: R = 1,000 null multiverses; null degeneracy = collapse. Inference: bootstrap B = 10,000 resamples of specifications; pairwise U-statistics for F and α-bar; p-values not reported (grid not independent). Functional diagnostics: agreement, functional instability = 1 - agreement, functional gap = F - (1 - agreement), Cohen's kappa, accuracy. Structural variance: REML over log10(size). Discovery families: edge-attribution patching (R8X), integrated edge gradients (B3Q); optimal ablation (C4Y) unsupported. Claim map G7U maps discovery output C(s) ⊆ E to structured Annex IV statements. Edge set size |E| = 32,491. Components: 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 total; text also says output receives 157 non-terminal sources (inconsistency flagged). For block index b, attention receives 1+13b sources at three input slots per each of 12 heads. Circuit instability D(s_i,s_j) = 1 - Jaccard(C_i,C_j); ̅J is mean Jaccard over unordered pairs. Claim instability F = 1 - Σ_c n_c(n_c-1) / [N(N-1)] (Gini–Simpson); within-group F_within(G) formula given. Ceiling: F ≤ 1 - 1/k; observed classes k=9 → ceiling 0.8889; observed fraction of ceiling 82.3% → observed F ≈ 0.731. Total claim-producing specifications: 7,561. Ablation operators: 7 levels (read-corruption nested); granularity: COARSE/MEDIUM/FINE. Null multiverses R=1,000; bootstrap B=10,000. Structural diagnostic: median D = 0.960. Functional diagnostic: Cohen's kappa = 0.0146. Earlier note: authors claim discovered circuits outperform size-matched random null A6N, but cited numbers in Sec.7.5 (0.2746 vs 0.4230; 0.2706 vs 0.3822) appear inconsistent with that claim.

Section G7U defines the claim mapping and reports sensitivity of F to size-binning choices. Size bins follow a committed calibration on a measured node-count curve (not tuned to F). Table 1 values: committed bins F=0.7316; all thresholds ×0.5: 0.7448; ×0.8: 0.7435; ×0.9: 0.7394; ×1.1: 0.7289; ×1.25: 0.7314; ×1.5: 0.7308; ×2: 0.7232; equal thirds: 0.7018; deciles: 0.7719; no size term (E7R): 0.5733. Sensitivity range across factor-four binnings reported as 0.70–0.77. Claim: four alternatives exceed the committed result (×0.5, ×0.8, ×0.9, deciles). Regulatory addressee mappings: D9P (overseer) orders layer band (early/middle/late), size class (sparse/moderate/distributed), ranked input segment; L3X (affected) leads with input segment. Resolutions: E7R=COARSE (coarsest), K8Z=MEDIUM, V2H=FINE; nested so refinements cannot contradict coarser statements. Claim map φ is pre-registered deterministic code. Carry-forward key earlier numbers and flags: specification tuple s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g) (axis-count ambiguity noted); claim map G7U; |E|=32,491; components: 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs (156) (earlier noted inconsistency with a 157 count flagged); total claim-producing specs 7,561; nulls R=1,000, bootstrap B=10,000; ceiling F≤1-1/k with k=9 → ceiling≈0.8889 and observed F≈0.731; structural diagnostic median D=0.960; functional diagnostic Cohen’s κ=0.0146. errors.explanation: The displayed formula for F is the without-replacement (finite-sample) form; in fact F = (N/(N-1))*(1 - \sum_c p_c^2). The maximum over distributions p_c (uniform p_c=1/k) gives F_max = (N/(N-1))*(1 - 1/k), which can exceed 1 - 1/k for finite N (and equals 1 when N=k and each class has n_c=1). Thus the statement "F \le 1-1/k" is mathematically incorrect for the estimator in Eq.2.

errors.explanation: The displayed formula for F is the without-replacement (finite-sample) form; in fact F = (N/(N-1))*(1 - \sum_c p_c^2). The maximum over distributions p_c (uniform p_c=1/k) gives F_max = (N/(N-1))*(1 - 1/k), which can exceed 1 - 1/k for finite N (and equals 1 when N=k and each class has n_c=1). Thus the statement "F \le 1-1/k" is mathematically incorrect for the estimator in Eq.2.

Analytic random Jaccard at median size 0.0031; expected random overlap at 500 edges ~0.008 (noted earlier mismatch). Key metrics: pooled discovered F = 0.7316 (95% CI 0.7247–0.7380). One script recomputes headline quantities (36 checks, 0 failures, F via three routes incl. brute-force pairs); another verifies every manuscript numeric token; test suite contains 343 tests; tables emitted directly.

final_notes: Model/task: GPT-2 small, indirect-object identification. Pre-registered 1,320-cell factorial grid; realized 15,840 specs; metric threshold kept 7,561 (~47.7%); 3,218 distinct circuits; Jaccard over 28,580,580 pairs. Key reported estimates: mean J̄ = 0.1396 (95% CI [0.1377, 0.1418]); pooled discovered flip rate F = 0.7316 (95% CI [0.7247, 0.7380]); pooled null F = 0.6774. H2 pooled discovered F = 0.7316; H3: size confounds pooled direction, fixing size reverses ordering (medium discovered ≈ 0.2746 vs null 0.4230; coarse 0.2706 vs 0.3822). Table 7: many specs collapse (null F = 0.0000 at ≥1,000 edges; discovered collapse at 5,000 and 10,000 edges; 2,692 specs produce no flips). Per-example agreement ≈0.6028 → instability ≈0.3972; gap to claim flip = 0.3344 (95% CI [0.3297,0.3394]). Raw agreement ≈0.60 (size-specific 0.52–0.92); accuracy 0.51–0.95. Reported overall Cohen's kappa 0.0146 vs per-size kappas 0.016–0.047 (inconsistency flagged). Filability protocol described. Instrument: one non-executing objective (one of seven); reported all 220 cells in that arm fail. Limitations: single model/task, omitted optimal ablation (measured F is a lower bound), high discard rate (52.3%), metric-imbalanced discard rates, bootstrap CI limits for small groups. Reproducibility claims in final part: prereg commit 'prereg-p1-confirmatory'; single environment across 1,320 cells; archive matched git (22/22 files identical); analysis runs without GPU; verification: 36 checks, 0 failures; F derived by three routes including brute-force; second script checks every numeric token and emits tables from stored results; test suite contains 343 tests. Contradiction: manuscript contains numeric/arithmetic mismatches (e.g. use of 0.1377 vs mean 0.1396 and kappa inconsistencies) despite the claim that all numeric tokens were automatically verified, and despite claim of 0 verification failures.

Confirmatory study on GPT-2 small for indirect-object identification. Pre-registered crossed multiverse: 15,840 specifications. Deterministic claim maps produce structured Annex IV statements; 7,561 specs produced a claim (~47.7%). Modal share π* = 0.411 (paper reports ~6,516 specs when applied to full-spec denominator). Observed flip rate F ≈ 0.7316 (reported 73.2%, 95% CI [0.725,0.738]). Standardising the evaluation metric reduces F to 0.594. Holding circuit size fixed reduces F to ~0.271 (95% CI [0.255,0.286]); fixed-size flip reported ~0.2746 (discovered) vs 0.4230 (random) in Sec.7.5. Circuits are structurally near-disjoint: median pairwise Jaccard overlap ≈ 4%. Functionally uncorrelated: Cohen’s κ ≈ 0.0146–0.015. Functional instability (1 − agreement) = 0.3972 pooled and 0.4777 for smallest circuits (Sec.7.6). Filability rule: evidence filable at tolerance α iff π* ≥ 1 − α; with π* = 0.411 the study reports failure to meet filability for any plausible α. Formalism (this part): specification s = (o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). Discovery returns C(s) ⊂ E with |E| = 32,491 edges. Closed-form edge breakdown: attention in block b receives from 1+13b sources at 3 input slots for each of 12 heads; MLP_b receives from those sources plus its own block’s heads; output receives from all 157 non-terminal sources. Components counted: 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 components. Circuit instability D(s_i,s_j) = 1 − |C_i ∩ C_j|/|C_i ∪ C_j| (mean Jaccard ̄J). Claim instability F = 1 − (Σ_c n_c(n_c − 1))/(N(N − 1)) (Gini–Simpson); modal share π* = max_c n_c / N. Within-group flip F_within(G) given by Eq.3 reduces to Eq.2 when G empty. Stated ceiling F ≤ 1 − 1/k; with k=9 observed classes ceiling = 0.8889 and observed F is ~82.3% of that. Unit tests compared Eq.2 to brute-force. Bootstrap B = 10,000; random-null multiverses R = 1,000. Design limits: single model, single task, seed selects sampled prompts.

Pre-registered 1,320-cell factorial grid realized 15,840 specs; metric threshold left 7,561 kept (~47.7%), 3,218 distinct circuits; Jaccard computed over 28,580,580 pairs. H3: distributions separated but pooled direction confounded by circuit size; holding size fixed reverses ordering (medium discovered ≈ 0.2746 vs null 0.4230; coarse 0.2706 vs 0.3822). Key estimates: mean J̄ = 0.1396 (95% CI [0.1377, 0.1418]); pooled discovered flip rate F = 0.7316 (95% CI [0.7247, 0.7380]); pooled null F = 0.6774. H2 pooled discovered flip rate F = 0.7316 (95% CI [0.7247,0.7380]). H3: size confounds pooled direction; fixing size reverses ordering (medium discovered ≈ 0.2746 vs null 0.4230; coarse 0.2706 vs 0.3822). Table 7: many specs collapse to single class (null F = 0.0000 at ≥1,000 edges; discovered collapse at 5,000 and 10,000 edges — n=625 and 2,067; total 2,692 specs produce no flips). Pooled per-example functional agreement ≈0.6028 → instability ≈0.3972; gap to claim flip = 0.3344 (95% CI [0.3297, 0.3394]). Reported raw agreement ≈0.60 (size-specific 0.52–0.92); accuracy 0.51–0.95. Flagged inconsistency: reported overall Cohen's kappa 0.0146 vs per-size kappas 0.016–0.047. Filability protocol: declare S, publish deterministic φ, compute π* = max_c n_c/N and F (Eq.2); filable if π* ≥ 1−α; report π*, F, discards. This part asserts metric "removes 0.1377" from 0.7316 to give 0.5939 (CI [0.5803,0.6063]) — but that contradicts the paper's earlier mean J̄ and CI arithmetic (see error). Also: instrument has one non-executing objective (one of seven; reported all 220 cells in that arm fail). Limitations noted: one model/task, omitted optimal ablation (measured F is lower bound), high discard rate (52.3%), metric-imbalanced discard rates, bootstrap CI limits for small groups.

Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Pre-registered crossed design for GPT-2 small (Q7V) on indirect-object identification (Z4K); committed but unrun second-model plan: Pythia-160m (M9B). Deterministic code G7U maps discovered circuits to structured Annex IV statements; 7,561 claim-producing specifications; pairwise claim disagreement F = 0.7316 (pooled). Removing size from statements and conditioning on size reduces disagreement to 0.2706. Discovered circuits outperform size-matched random null (A6N) at fixed size; pooled comparison reverses. Graph: factorised (query/key/value) with |E| = 32,491 edges; 12 blocks, 12 heads/block (144 heads), 12 MLPs. Specification s = (objective o, ablation operator a, corruption distribution d, metric m, size threshold τ, prompt variant P, seed r, granularity g). Ablation operators: 7 total (five read corruption, two do not); d nested within operators that read corruption. Granularities: COARSE (E7R), MEDIUM (K8Z), FINE (V2H). Metrics (four): comprehensiveness (T9V), KL divergence (H2W), logit difference (N6C), sufficiency (U4J). Discovery: crossed grid, discovery cell counted before metric/threshold/statement reporting; metric-relative threshold rule; retention/discard rates tracked; one objective arm failed (MSE/integral target runtime error). Statistical tooling: Jaccard α = intersection/union, α-bar = mean over unordered pairs; D = 1 - Jaccard; F defined in Gini–Simpson form (pair disagreement); G and F_within(G) for conditioning; pi* = max_class_share; Y3W filability requires pi* >= 1 - alpha (alpha = filing tolerance). Nulls: R = 1,000 null multiverses; null degeneracy = collapse. Inference: bootstrap B = 10,000 resamples of specifications; pairwise U-statistics for F and α-bar; p-values not reported (grid not independent). Functional diagnostics: agreement, functional instability = 1 - agreement, functional gap = F - (1 - agreement), Cohen's kappa, accuracy. Structural variance: REML over log10(size). Discovery families: edge-attribution patching (R8X), integrated edge gradients (B3Q); optimal ablation (C4Y) unsupported. Pre-registration artifacts: deviations file, six-cell validation slice, environment fingerprint, content-addressed git tree, tag 'prereg-p1-confirmatory'. GPU not required.

steps.notes_before: Paper: Explanation Multiplicity (pre-registered). Model: GPT-2 small (Q7V). Specification tuple s = (o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g) — eight axes (axis-count ambiguity noted). Claim map G7U maps discovery output C(s) ⊆ E to structured Annex IV statements. Edge set size |E| = 32,491. Components: 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 total; text also says output receives 157 non-terminal sources (inconsistency flagged). For block index b, attention receives 1+13b sources at three input slots per each of 12 heads. Circuit instability D(s_i,s_j) = 1 - Jaccard(C_i,C_j); ̅J is mean Jaccard over unordered pairs. Claim instability F = 1 - Σ_c n_c(n_c-1) / [N(N-1)] (Gini–Simpson); within-group F_within(G) formula given. Ceiling: F ≤ 1 - 1/k; observed classes k=9 → ceiling 0.8889; observed fraction of ceiling 82.3% → observed F ≈ 0.731. Total claim-producing specifications: 7,561. Ablation operators: 7 levels (read-corruption nested); granularity: COARSE/MEDIUM/FINE. Null multiverses R=1,000; bootstrap B=10,000. Structural diagnostic: median D = 0.960. Functional diagnostic: Cohen's kappa = 0.0146. Earlier note: authors claim discovered circuits outperform size-matched random null A6N, but cited numbers in Sec.7.5 (0.2746 vs 0.4230; 0.2706 vs 0.3822) appear inconsistent with that claim.

Section G7U defines the claim mapping and reports sensitivity of F to size-binning choices. Size bins follow a committed calibration on a measured node-count curve (not tuned to F). Table 1 values: committed bins F=0.7316; all thresholds ×0.5: 0.7448; ×0.8: 0.7435; ×0.9: 0.7394; ×1.1: 0.7289; ×1.25: 0.7314; ×1.5: 0.7308; ×2: 0.7232; equal thirds: 0.7018; deciles: 0.7719; no size term (E7R): 0.5733. Sensitivity range across factor-four binnings reported as 0.70–0.77. Claim: four alternatives exceed the committed result (×0.5, ×0.8, ×0.9, deciles). Regulatory addressee mappings: D9P (overseer) orders layer band (early/middle/late), size class (sparse/moderate/distributed), ranked input segment; L3X (affected) leads with input segment. Resolutions: E7R=COARSE (coarsest), K8Z=MEDIUM, V2H=FINE; nested so refinements cannot contradict coarser statements. Claim map φ is pre-registered deterministic code. Carry-forward key earlier numbers and flags: specification tuple s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g) (axis-count ambiguity noted); claim map G7U; |E|=32,491; components: 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs (156) (earlier noted inconsistency with a 157 count flagged); total claim-producing specs 7,561; nulls R=1,000, bootstrap B=10,000; ceiling F≤1-1/k with k=9 → ceiling≈0.8889 and observed F≈0.731; structural diagnostic median D=0.960; functional diagnostic Cohen’s κ=0.0146. Section 6 (Method): Grid axes — 7 objectives; 7 operators (5 operators read 4 corruption distributions each; 2 operators ignore corruption) ; 4 metrics (T9V, H2W (KL), N6C (logit diff), U4J); 3 thresholds; 2 prompt variants; 5 seeds. Operator×corruption combos = 5*4 + 2 = 22. Reported counts: discovery cells = 1,540; pre-registered specifications = 18,480 (consistent with 7*22*4*3*2*5 = 18,480 when corruption nesting is applied). Specifications admitting no circuit = 8,279 → claim-producing (admitting circuits) = 7,561; overall discard rate = 52.3%.
