final_notes: Study of circuit-level interpretability / Y3W robustness in one model (Q7V / GPT-2 small). Original grid: 7,561 claim-producing specs → 3,218 distinct circuits. Pooled discovery F = 0.7316 (95% CI 0.7247–0.7380). Pairwise D quantiles: 1% 0.196, 25% 0.788, median 0.960, 75% 0.998. Median circuit size 200 edges; median shared-edge fraction 4%; analytic random Jaccard at median size 0.0031; expected random overlap for 500-edge ≈0.008; observed/chance overlap ≈45×. Many specs produce no flips: 2,692/7,561. Fixed-size (size-standardised) F = 0.2706 (95% CI 0.2550–0.2859). Pooled vs A6N: pooled 0.7316 vs A6N 0.6774; but fixed-size discovery < A6N for examples (K8Z 0.2746 vs A6N 0.4230; E7R 0.2706 vs A6N 0.3822). A6N degeneracy >1,000 edges; discovery collapses at 5k–10k edges. Functional diagnostics: pooled per-example agreement 0.6028; pooled functional instability 0.3972; smallest-circuit instability 0.4777. Cohen’s kappa pooled 0.0146 (per-size 0.016–0.047). REML: ablation–corruption interaction explains 78.8% structural variance. Metric-standardised percentage disagreement 59.4%; axis-standardised residual reductions: axis metric 0.5939 (removes 0.1377), seed 0.7307 (removes 0.0009). Y3W protocol: declare S and φ, compute π* = max_c n_c/N over S and F; pass iff π* ≥ 1−α; report π*, F, discard rates, within-group decompositions. Limitations: one model/one task (plan M9B unrun); circuit size treated as outcome not axis; C4Y (optimal ablation) not in instrument space (measured F is a lower bound); high/uneven discard and tooling immaturity; bootstrap invalid for some small families (2–5 specs) where unusable intervals were replaced by point estimates. Reproducibility: public commit tag prereg-p1-confirmatory; every reported number traces to config/seed/environment fingerprint; archive verification found one environment across all 1,320 confirmatory cells; content-addressed compare recovered code commit vs git tree (22/22 files identical); analysis needs no GPU. Test suite: one script recomputes headlines (36 checks, 0 failures; F via three routes incl brute-force pairs), another verifies manuscript numeric tokens; tables emitted directly; suite contains 343 tests.

Paper: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability — Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026. Central claim: circuit-derived regulatory evidence can fail Y3W within plausible tolerances; φ is pre-registered deterministic code. Formalism: spec s = (o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). Circuit output C(s) ⊂ E; for Q7V (GPT-2 small) |E| = 32,491. F (Gini–Simpson) committed 0.7316 (observed ≈0.731); Y3W ceiling = 1−1/k with k=9 → 0.8889 (observed fraction of ceiling 82.3%). Table 1 alternative binnings (committed 0.7316; equal thirds 0.7018; deciles 0.7719; 'no size term (E7R)' 0.5733); noted inconsistency in claimed sensitivity phrasing and E7R labelling. Methods (this part): model Q7V (GPT-2 small), task Z4K (indirect object identification). Grid factors: 7 objectives, 7 operators (5 read corruption, 2 do not), 4 corruption distributions nested within the 5 operators, 4 metrics (T9V=comprehensiveness, H2W=KL, N6C=logit diff, U4J=sufficiency), 3 thresholds, 2 prompt variants, 5 seeds → discovery cells = 7*(5*4+2)*2*5 = 1,540; pre-registered specifications = 1,540*4*3 = 18,480. Discovery methods: R8X (edge attribution patching) and B3Q (integrated edge gradients). Statistics: no spec-level p-values; nonparametric bootstrap resamples specifications B=10,000; F and J-bar are pairwise U-statistics. Two pre-specified exclusions: one objective entirely failed (runtime error) → 220 failed objective cells; realised objectives 6; realised discovery cells 1,320; realised specifications 15,840. Specifications admitting no circuit: 8,279 (discard rate ≈52.3%); surviving specs = 7,561. Metric-specific kept counts (out of 3,960 per metric): T9V kept 3,947 (discard 13; discard rate 0.003), H2W kept 1,467 (discard 2,493; 0.630), N6C kept 1,270 (discard 2,690; 0.679), U4J kept 877 (discard 3,083; 0.779). Designed T9V composition 25%; surviving T9V composition ≈52%.

final_notes: Model/task: GPT-2 small, indirect-object ID. Pre-registration: timestamped commit 'prereg-p1-confirmatory' made before confirmatory sweep; realized 1,320 cells → 15,840 specs; metric threshold retained 7,561 (~47.7%), discarded 52.3%. Distinct circuits: 3,218; mean Jaccard J̄ = 0.1396 (95% CI [0.1377,0.1418]). Pooled flip F = 0.7316 (95% CI [0.7247,0.7380]); pooled null = 0.6774 (R=1,000 random multiverses). Metric reported to remove 0.1377 from 0.7316 → leaving 0.5939 (CI 0.5803–0.6063). Circuit-size confound: holding size fixed reverses pooled ordering and reduces discovered F to ≈0.2746. Collapse behavior: null predictions collapse at ≥1,000 edges (null F=0); discovered collapse at 5k/10k edges (n=625 and 2,067; F=0); 2,692 specs produce no flips. H4 pooled: per-example agreement ≈0.6028 → instability ≈0.3972; gap to claim flip = 0.3344 (95% CI [0.3297,0.3394]) > 0.10 but effect fails at many sizes; agreement range ≈0.52–0.92; accuracy 0.51–0.95. Kappa: overall κ≈0.0146 vs per-size 0.016–0.047. Instrumentation: one of seven documented discovery-objective arms fails on canonical task (all 220 cells), reported discarded. Filability protocol (Section 8): declare S and deterministic claim map φ, compute π* = max_c n_c/N, claim filable if π* ≥ 1−α; report π*, F, discard rates, within-group decompositions. Paper notes measured F is a lower bound (omitted “optimal ablation”). Reproducibility claims (Section 11): results archive verifies a single environment across all 1,320 cells; content-addressed archive/git comparison: 22 of 22 files identical; analysis layer runs without GPU; verification script recomputes headline quantities: 36 checks, 0 failures; F derived by three routes including brute-force pairwise; second script checks every numeric token; tables emitted from results; test suite contains 343 tests.

Context: confirmatory study on GPT-2 small (indirect object identification). Grid/multiverse: N = 15,840 specifications. 7,561 specifications produce a claim (~47.7%).

Claims & mapping: deterministic claim map φ maps each discovered circuit to a structured Annex IV statement (three nested granularities: COARSE, MEDIUM, FINE). Two claim maps: φ_overseer and φ_affected. Modal claim share π* = max_c n_c / N = 0.411 (≈6,516 specs).

Main reported statistics: claim flip rate F = 73.2% (probability two distinct specifications yield different statements). Standardising the evaluation metric reduces F to 59.4%. Removing circuit size from the claim (holding size fixed) reduces F to 27.1%. Median circuit Jaccard overlap = 4%. Functional agreement (Cohen’s kappa adjusted) ≈ 0; functional instability ≈ 1. Functional gap = F − functional instability.

Method/choices: Seven discovery objectives documented, six executed. Circuit = subset of model edges; component = attention head or MLP. Evaluation metrics include KL/logit diff/sufficiency, accuracy, comprehensiveness. Structural variance: REML decomposition on log10(selected circuit size). Calibration rule maps node-count curve to size bins (labels: sparse/moderate/distributed). Bootstrap: B = 10,000 resamples of specifications (CIs conditional on grid). Random-null multiverses: R = 1,000.

Pre-registered outcomes: H2 (F > 0.20 with CI lower bound > 0.20), H3 (not separated from random null), H4 (F − (1 − agreement) > 0.10). Filability: evidence filable at tolerance α iff π* ≥ 1 − α.

Filability rule: evidence filable at tolerance α iff π* ≥ 1 − α; with π* = 0.411 the study reports failure to meet filability for any plausible α. Formalism (this part): specification s = (o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). Discovery returns C(s) ⊂ E with |E| = 32,491 edges. Components counted: 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 components. Circuit instability D(s_i,s_j) = 1 − |C_i ∩ C_j|/|C_i ∪ C_j| (mean Jaccard ̄J). Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Pre-registered crossed design for GPT-2 small (Q7V) on indirect-object identification (Z4K); committed but unrun second-model plan: Pythia-160m (M9B). Deterministic code G7U maps discovered circuits to structured Annex IV statements; 7,561 claim-producing specifications; pairwise claim disagreement F = 0.7316 (pooled). Removing size from statements and conditioning on size reduces disagreement to 0.2706. Discovered circuits outperform size-matched random null (A6N) at fixed size; pooled comparison reverses. Graph: factorised (query/key/value) with |E| = 32,491 edges; 12 blocks, 12 heads/block (144 heads), 12 MLPs. Specification s = (objective o, ablation operator a, corruption distribution d, metric m, size threshold τ, prompt variant P, seed r, granularity g). Ablation operators: 7 total (five read corruption, two do not); d nested within operators that read corruption. Granularities: COARSE (E7R), MEDIUM (K8Z), FINE (V2H). Metrics (four): comprehensiveness (T9V), KL divergence (H2W), logit difference (N6C), sufficiency (U4J). Discovery: crossed grid, discovery cell counted before metric/threshold/statement reporting; metric-relative threshold rule; retention/discard rates tracked; one objective arm failed (MSE/integral target runtime error). Statistical tooling: Jaccard α = intersection/union, α-bar = mean over unordered pairs; D = 1 - Jaccard; F defined in Gini–Simpson form (pair disagreement); G and F_within(G) for conditioning; pi* = max_class_share; Y3W filability requires pi* >= 1 - alpha (alpha = filing tolerance). Nulls: R = 1,000 null multiverses; null degeneracy = collapse. Inference: bootstrap B = 10,000 resamples of specifications; pairwise U-statistics for F and α-bar; p-values not reported (grid not independent). Functional diagnostics: agreement, functional instability = 1 - agreement, functional gap = F - (1 - agreement), Cohen's kappa, accuracy. Structural variance: REML over log10(size). Discovery families: edge-attribution patching (R8X), integrated edge gradients (B3Q); optimal ablation (C4Y) unsupported. Pre-registration artifacts: deviations file, six-cell validation slice, environment fingerprint, content-addressed git tree, tag 'prereg-p1-confirmatory'. GPU not required.

steps.notes_before: Paper: Explanation Multiplicity (pre-registered). Model: GPT-2 small (Q7V). Specification tuple s = (o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g) — eight axes (axis-count ambiguity noted). Claim map G7U maps discovery output C(s) ⊆ E to structured Annex IV statements. Edge set size |E| = 32,491. Components: 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 total; text also says output receives 157 non-terminal sources (inconsistency flagged). For block index b, attention receives 1+13b sources at three input slots per each of 12 heads. Circuit instability D(s_i,s_j) = 1 - Jaccard(C_i,C_j); ̅J is mean Jaccard over unordered pairs. Claim instability F = 1 - Σ_c n_c(n_c-1) / [N(N-1)] (Gini–Simpson); within-group F_within(G) formula given. Ceiling: F ≤ 1 - 1/k; observed classes k=9 → ceiling 0.8889; observed fraction of ceiling 82.3% → observed F ≈ 0.731. Total claim-producing specifications: 7,561. Ablation operators: 7 levels (read-corruption nested); granularity: COARSE/MEDIUM/FINE. Null multiverses R=1,000; bootstrap B=10,000. Structural diagnostic: median D = 0.960. Functional diagnostic: Cohen's kappa = 0.0146. Earlier note: authors claim discovered circuits outperform size-matched random null A6N, but cited numbers in Sec.7.5 (0.2746 vs 0.4230; 0.2706 vs 0.3822) appear inconsistent with that claim.

Section G7U defines the claim mapping and reports sensitivity of F to size-binning choices. Size bins follow a committed calibration on a measured node-count curve (not tuned to F). Table 1 values: committed bins F=0.7316; all thresholds ×0.5: 0.7448; ×0.8: 0.7435; ×0.9: 0.7394; ×1.1: 0.7289; ×1.25: 0.7314; ×1.5: 0.7308; ×2: 0.7232; equal thirds: 0.7018; deciles: 0.7719; no size term (E7R): 0.5733. Sensitivity range across factor-four binnings reported as 0.70–0.77. Claim: four alternatives exceed the committed result (×0.5, ×0.8, ×0.9, deciles). Regulatory addressee mappings: D9P (overseer) orders layer band (early/middle/late), size class (sparse/moderate/distributed), ranked input segment; L3X (affected) leads with input segment. Resolutions: E7R=COARSE (coarsest), K8Z=MEDIUM, V2H=FINE; nested so refinements cannot contradict coarser statements. Claim map φ is pre-registered deterministic code. Carry-forward key earlier numbers and flags: specification tuple s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g) (axis-count ambiguity noted); claim map G7U; |E|=32,491; components: 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs (156) (earlier noted inconsistency with a 157 count flagged); total claim-producing specs 7,561; nulls R=1,000, bootstrap B=10,000; ceiling F≤1-1/k with k=9 → ceiling≈0.8889 and observed F≈0.731; structural diagnostic median D=0.960; functional diagnostic Cohen’s κ=0.0146. Previously flagged potential inconsistency: authors' claim circuits outperform size-matched random null A6N (Sec.7.5 numbers looked inconsistent).

Section 6 (Method): Grid axes — 7 objectives; 7 operators (5 operators read 4 corruption distributions each; 2 operators ignore corruption) ; 4 metrics (T9V, H2W (KL), N6C (logit diff), U4J); 3 thresholds; 2 prompt variants; 5 seeds. Operator×corruption combos = 5*4 + 2 = 22. Reported counts: discovery cells = 1,540; pre-registered specifications = 18,480 (consistent with 7*22*4*3*2*5 = 18,480 when corruption nesting is applied). Discovery cell appears to index objectives × operator-corruption × prompts × seeds (7*22*2*5 = 1,540); pre-registered specs = discovery cells × 4 metrics × 3 thresholds = 18,480. Methods used: R8X (edge-attribution patching) and B3Q (integrated edge gradients); lineage and corruption sources cited. Pre-registration: plan and directional abstracts committed; append-only deviations file recorded. Statistics: no specification-level p-values; nonparametric bootstrap resamples specifications (B = 10,000); F and J̄ are pairwise U-statistics; CIs condition on the grid. Exclusions: one objective fails fully — "Failed objective cells" = 220 → realised objectives = 6; realised discovery cells = 1,320; realised specifications = 15,840. Specifications admitting no circuit = 8,279 → claim-producing (admitting circuits) = 7,561; overall discard rate = 52.3%. Metric-specific retention (kept / discarded / discard rate): T9V 3,947 / 13 / 0.003; H2W 1,467 / 2,493 / 0.630; N6C 1,270 / 2,690 / 0.679; U4J 877 / 3,083 / 0.779. final_notes: Context: GPT-2 small, indirect-object identification. Final counts: 7,561 surviving specs (3,218 distinct circuits). Key pooled numbers: discovered claim-flip F = 0.7316 (95% CI 0.7247–0.7380); π* = 0.4109; mean J̄ = 0.1396 (95% CI 0.1377–0.1418); median per-pair J ≈ 0.04; median circuit size ≈ 200 edges. Per-example functional agreement = 0.6028 (instability 0.3972); gap to claim flip rate = 0.3344 (95% CI 0.3297–0.3394). Pooled discovered collapse: 2,692 specs contribute no flips; instability concentrated below 2,000 edges (main effect 500–2,000). Size-matched discovered vs null ≈ 0.27 vs ≈ 0.38–0.42; holding size fixed discovered F ≈ 0.2706 (95% CI 0.2550–0.2859). REML variance decomposition: 78.8% structural (ablation×corruption), 11.5% residual, 4.4% ablation, 4.1% threshold, 0.7% metric. Standardising metric removes 0.1377 from 0.7316 → residual F = 0.5939. Limitations: one model/one task; second-model replication pre-registered but not run (Pythia-160m, 924-cell grid; seed axis reduced); circuit size is an outcome (threshold rule) and strongly affects pooled quantities; multiverse equals implemented library (optimal ablation omitted → measured F is a lower bound). Discard rate high (52.3%) and surviving pool metric-imbalanced; bootstrap CIs for some conditioned families invalid and reported as diagnostics/point estimates. Reproducibility: prereg commit tagged prereg-p1-confirmatory; confirmatory sweep ran under a single environment across all 1,320 cells (verified from results archive); code commit recovered via content-addressed comparison, 22/22 files identical; analysis layer runs without a GPU. Verification: script recomputes every headline quantity (36 checks, 0 failures), F computed via three routes including brute-force pairwise; second script checks every numeric token in manuscript; every table emitted from results; test suite = 343 tests.

Reproducibility (this part): single environment across all 1,320 cells verified; archive recovered code 22/22 files identical; verification script: 36 checks, 0 failures; F derived three ways including brute-force; second script allegedly checks every numeric token and emits tables from stored results; test suite 343 tests. Internal inconsistencies flagged earlier and still relevant: Discussion arithmetic mismatch (paper: "removes 0.1377 from 0.7316 leaving 0.5939 [0.5803,0.6063]" vs arithmetic from reported mean 0.1396 → 0.5920 and CI [0.5829,0.6003]); and a count mismatch ('one of seven' arms asserted elsewhere vs pre-registered six axes / 220-per-axis). Random-null multiverses: R = 1,000.

Pre-registered outcomes: H2 (F > 0.20 with CI lower bound > 0.20), H3 (not separated from random null), H4 (F − (1 − agreement) > 0.10). Filability: evidence filable at tolerance α iff π* ≥ 1 − α.

Filability protocol (new): filer must declare specification space S (analytic axes and defensible levels, with citations), declare deterministic claim map φ as published code (not an LLM), compute π* = max_c n_c/N over S and compute F using Equation 2, and a claim is filable at tolerance α if π* ≥ 1−α. Filing that cannot state its own π* is an assertion, not an audit; regulator need not pick correct analytic choice — protocol is implementable because filer must declare space and report how much of it agrees.

Paper: "Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability." Pre-registered crossed design on GPT-2 small (Pythia-160m arm planned/unrun). 7,561 claim-producing specifications; 7 ablation ops (5 read-corruption, 2 no-read); granularities COARSE/MEDIUM/FINE. Discovery families include edge-attribution patching (R8X) and integrated edge gradients (B3Q). Discovery counted before metric/threshold/statement; metric-relative threshold rule; nulls R=1,000 multiverses; bootstrap B=10,000. One objective arm failed (MSE runtime error). Seed controls prompt sampling; no scale claims.

Specification tuple: s = (o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). Claim map G7U maps discovery output C(s) ⊆ E (edges) to structured Annex IV statements φ(C).

Model/graph: Q7V (GPT-2 small). |E| = 32,491 (instrument + computation-order confirmed). 12 blocks, 12 heads/block → 144 attention heads, 12 MLPs → 156 components. For block index b: attention receives 1+13b sources at three input slots per head. MLP b receives those sources plus its block’s heads. Output receives all 157 non-terminal sources (components = 156; extra non-terminal source implied).

Definitions/formalism:
- Circuit instability D(s_i,s_j) = 1 − |C_i ∩ C_j| / |C_i ∪ C_j| (one minus Jaccard). ̅J = mean Jaccard over unordered pairs.
- Claim instability F = 1 − [Σ_c n_c(n_c−1)] / [N(N−1)] (Gini–Simpson pair-disagreement; distinct draws without replacement).
- Conditioned within-axis: F_within(G) = 1 − [Σ_g Σ_c n_{g,c}(n_{g,c}−1)] / [Σ_g n_g(n_g−1)].
- Ceiling (Y3W): for k claim classes, F ≤ 1 − 1/k. Observed k = 9 → ceiling = 0.8889. Observed F ≈ 0.7316 = 82.3% of ceiling.

Key reported outcomes to keep for later checks: pooled F = 0.7316; conditioning on size reduces F to 0.2706; median structural D = 0.960; Cohen’s κ = 0.0146. Main claim: circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W criterion; standardisation/size controls do not remove failure.

Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability. Author: Ajay Pravin Mahale. Date: 12 Aug 2026. Domain: circuit-level interpretability. Main claim (from preface): circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across plausibly acceptable tolerances: competent analysts using the same system and tool can produce incompatible statements under different defensible settings. Introduction notes: auditing framed as requiring two auditors to reach the same conclusion (a commissioning requirement, not an ML definition). Regulatory motivation: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (consolidated text amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, CELEX 02024R1689-20260727; read 11 Aug 2026) asks for “general logic” (Annex IV 2(b)) and measures to facilitate interpretation (2(e)); Article 86(1) asks for clear explanations of the AI system’s role. Mechanistic interpretability (circuit discovery) returns a subgraph said to explain behavior; filing such accounts presumes compatibility between analysts. Study design: pre-registered crossed design using published implementations only; circuits are converted into structured Annex IV statements deterministically. Controls standardize individual axes, remove claim-size dependence, and condition on size. Key reported empirical result: three pooled statistics invert when selected objects differ in size. Paper does not propose improved discovery methods—the objection targets the standard assumed when filing current evidence; uses a standards-body decision rule to measure regulatory-claim movement across defensible specifications.

errors.evidence: "The metric is the biggest lever. It removes 0.1377 from a 0.7316 flip rate." (this part) vs earlier notes: "fixing size drops F 0.7316→0.2746" and "H3: strong size dependence — ... medium discovered 0.2746 ... coarse discovered 0.2706"

errors.claim: "leaving 0.5939, CI 0.5803 to 0.6063 (Table 6, Evaluation metric)."

Earlier reported values in notes: "H2 pooled discovered flip rate F = 0.7316 [0.7247,0.7380]" and "P0 mean J = 0.1396 [0.1377,0.1418]". Propagating bounds gives F_lo - J_hi = 0.7247 - 0.1418 = 0.5829 and F_hi - J_lo = 0.7380 - 0.1377 = 0.6003, i.e. CI ≈ [0.5829, 0.6003], not [0.5803, 0.6063].
errors.explanation: The reported point subtraction uses 0.1377 (the lower CI bound of J) rather than the reported mean 0.1396, and the stated CI for the difference does not match the interval obtained by combining the earlier reported CIs for F and J. final_notes: Key results: P0 mean J = 0.1396 [0.1377, 0.1418]. H2 pooled discovered flip rate F = 0.7316 [0.7247, 0.7380] (pooled vs size-matched null 0.6774). Strong size dependence (H3): within-size discovered ≈0.2746 (medium) vs null 0.4230; coarse ≈0.2706 vs null 0.3822 — controlling size reduces pooled F dramatically (~0.7316 → ~0.2746). H4 pooled functional gap 0.3344 [0.3297, 0.3394]; per-example agreement 0.6028 → instability 0.3972. Pooled tests pass but many size-specific tests fail; pooled effect concentrated in 500–2,000-edge band; instability concentrated <2,000 edges. Filability protocol: require S and deterministic claim map φ, compute π* = max_c n_c/N and F; filable iff π* ≥ 1−α; report π*, F, discard rates, within-group decompositions. Limitations recorded: single model/task; planned 924-cell replication and second task unrun; circuit-size thresholding distorts pooled F; optimal ablation omitted so measured F is a lower bound; overall discard rate reported 52.3% and surviving pool is metric-imbalanced; bootstrap invalid for very small conditioning groups. Metric standardisation claimed to "remove 0.1377" from F with derived CI centered at 0.5939 (CI 0.5803–0.6063). Reproducibility (part 11): preregistered commit 'prereg-p1-confirmatory'; results archive verifies a single environment across 1,320 cells (one objective/220 cells fully discarded); content-addressed match to code commit: 22/22 files identical; analysis layer runs without GPU; verification script: 36 checks, 0 failures; F computed by three routes (incl. brute-force pairwise); second script checks every numeric token and emits tables from results; test suite contains 343 tests.

Context: confirmatory study on GPT-2 small (indirect object identification). Grid/multiverse: N = 15,840 specifications. 7,561 specifications produce a claim (~47.7%).

Claims & mapping: deterministic claim map φ maps each discovered circuit to a structured Annex IV statement (three nested granularities: COARSE, MEDIUM, FINE). Two claim maps: φ_overseer and φ_affected. Modal claim share π* = max_c n_c / N = 0.411 (≈6,516 specs).

Random-null multiverses: R = 1,000.

Pre-registered outcomes: H2 (F > 0.20 with CI lower bound > 0.20), H3 (not separated from random null), H4 (F − (1 − agreement) > 0.10). Filability: evidence filable at tolerance α iff π* ≥ 1 − α.

Confirmatory study on GPT-2 small for indirect-object identification. Pre-registered crossed multiverse: 15,840 specifications. Deterministic claim maps produce structured Annex IV statements; 7,561 specs produced a claim (~47.7%). Modal share π* = 0.411 (paper reports ~6,516 specs when applied to full-spec denominator). Observed flip rate F ≈ 0.7316 (reported 73.2%, 95% CI [0.725,0.738]). Standardising the evaluation metric reduces F to 0.594. Holding circuit size fixed reduces F to ~0.271 (95% CI [0.255,0.286]); fixed-size flip reported ~0.2746 (discovered) vs 0.4230 (random) in Sec.7.5. Circuits are structurally near-disjoint: median pairwise Jaccard overlap ≈ 4%. Functionally uncorrelated: Cohen’s κ ≈ 0.0146–0.015. Functional instability (1 − agreement) = 0.3972 pooled and 0.4777 for smallest circuits (Sec.7.6). Filability rule: evidence filable at tolerance α iff π* ≥ 1 − α; with π* = 0.411 the study reports failure to meet filability for any plausible α. Formalism (this part): specification s = (o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). Discovery returns C(s) ⊂ E with |E| = 32,491 edges. Closed-form edge breakdown: attention in block b receives from 1+13b sources at 3 input slots for each of 12 heads; MLP_b receives from those sources plus its own block’s heads; output receives from all 157 non-terminal sources. Components counted: 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 components. Circuit instability D(s_i,s_j) = 1 − |C_i ∩ C_j|/|C_i ∪ C_j| (mean Jaccard ̄J). Claim instability F = 1 − (Σ_c n_c(n_c − 1))/(N(N − 1)) (Gini–Simpson); modal share π* = max_c n_c / N. Within-group flip F_within(G) given by Eq.3 reduces to Eq.2 when G empty. Stated ceiling F ≤ 1 − 1/k; with k=9 observed classes ceiling = 0.8889 and observed F is ~82.3% of that. Unit tests compared Eq.2 to brute-force. Bootstrap B = 10,000; random-null multiverses R = 1,000. Design limits: single model, single task, seed selects sampled prompts.

errors.claim: "Note the ceiling: F\leq 1-1/k for k claim classes, so a reported flip rate must be read against the number of classes the map can produce. With the nine classes observed here the ceiling is 0.8889, and the observed 0.7316 is 82.3% of it. F is not near one by construction."
errors.evidence: "Equation 2: F = 1 - \frac{\sum_{c} n_{c}(n_{c}-1)}{N(N-1)}" (the finite-sample Gini–Simpson form) and the quoted ceiling sentence above.
errors.explanation: The displayed formula for F is the without-replacement (finite-sample) form; in fact F = (N/(N-1))*(1 - \sum_c p_c^2). The maximum over distributions p_c (uniform p_c=1/k) gives F_max = (N/(N-1))*(1 - 1/k), which can exceed 1 - 1/k for finite N (and equals 1 when N=k and each class has n_c=1). Thus the statement "F \le 1-1/k" is mathematically incorrect for the estimator in Eq.2.

Paper: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Research question: whether mechanistic/circuit discovery evidence is robust to defensible analytic variation (two competent analysts, same system and tool, different defensible settings). Method: pre-registered crossed grid of 7 analytic axes (levels taken from published implementations); mapped each discovered circuit via a deterministic claim map to a structured Annex IV statement. Dataset/experiment: GPT-2 small on an indirect object identification task; 15,840 pre-registered specifications, of which 7,561 produced a claim. Main results: derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs (95% CI 0.725–0.738); modal claim covers 41.1% of the space. Standardising the most influential axis (evaluation metric) yields flip rate 59.4%. Removing circuit size from the claim and holding it fixed yields flip rate 27.1% (95% CI 0.255–0.286), still above the pre-registered threshold (threshold value not given here). Circuits are near-disjoint (median pairwise Jaccard overlap 4%) and functionally uncorrelated (Cohen's kappa 0.015) — authors argue instability is not merely one mechanism restated. They provide a filability criterion/protocol and report one of seven documented discovery objectives fails to execute on the library's canonical task. Study limitation: single model and single task; generalisability untested.

At fixed circuit size discovered circuits are more stable than a size-matched random null (0.2746 vs 0.4230). Functional instability: pooled 0.3972 and 0.4777 at the smallest circuits. Circuits are structurally near-disjoint (median pairwise Jaccard overlap 4%) and functionally uncorrelated (Cohen's κ ≈ 0.015; reported 0.0146). Authors argue seed effects reflect evaluation-set (prompt) sampling rather than model nondeterminism. Contributions: (i) pre-registered multiverse + deterministic Annex IV mapping; (ii) filability criterion + measured value on canonical task; (iii) instability survives controls (standardising axes, removing/holding size); (iv) methodological note on pooling statistics across specs selecting different circuit sizes. Limitation: one model, one task; generalisability untested.

errors.claim: "Note the ceiling: F\leq 1-1/k for k claim classes, so a reported flip rate must be read against the number of classes the map can produce. With the nine classes observed here the ceiling is 0.8889, and the observed 0.7316 is 82.3% of it. F is not near one by construction."
errors.evidence: "Equation 2: F = 1 - \frac{\sum_{c} n_{c}(n_{c}-1)}{N(N-1)}" (the finite-sample Gini–Simpson form) and the quoted ceiling sentence above.
errors.explanation: The displayed formula for F is the without-replacement (finite-sample) form; in fact F = (N/(N-1))*(1 - \sum_c p_c^2). The maximum over distributions p_c (uniform p_c=1/k) gives F_max = (N/(N-1))*(1 - 1/k), which can exceed 1 - 1/k for finite N (and equals 1 when N=k and each class has n_c=1). Thus the statement "F \le 1-1/k" is mathematically incorrect for the estimator in Eq.2.

Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability. Author: Ajay Pravin Mahale. Date: 12 Aug 2026. Domain: circuit-level interpretability. Main claim (from preface): circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across plausibly acceptable tolerances: competent analysts using the same system and tool can produce incompatible statements under different defensible settings. Limitation: applicability beyond the single model/task studied remains untested. Introduction notes: auditing framed as requiring two auditors to reach the same conclusion (a commissioning requirement, not an ML definition). Regulatory motivation: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (consolidated text amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, CELEX 02024R1689-20260727; read 11 Aug 2026) asks for “general logic” (Annex IV 2(b)) and measures to facilitate interpretation (2(e)); Article 86(1) asks for clear explanations of the AI system’s role. Mechanistic interpretability (circuit discovery) returns a subgraph said to explain behavior; filing such accounts presumes compatibility between analysts. Study design: pre-registered crossed design using published implementations only; circuits are converted into structured Annex IV statements deterministically. Controls standardize individual axes, remove claim-size dependence, and condition on size. Key reported empirical result: three pooled statistics invert when selected objects differ in size. Paper does not propose improved discovery methods—the objection targets the standard assumed when filing current evidence; uses a standards-body decision rule to measure regulatory-claim movement across defensible specifications.

Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability. Author/date: Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026. Domain: circuit-level (mechanistic) interpretability; regulatory filing focus. Main claim: circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across plausibly acceptable tolerances—competent analysts using the same system and tool can produce incompatible statements under different defensible settings. Limitation: single model/task only; broader applicability untested. Study design: pre-registered crossed design using published implementations only; circuits converted deterministically into structured Annex IV statements. Controls standardize individual axes, remove claim-size dependence, condition on size. Key empirical result noted earlier: three pooled statistics invert when selected objects differ in size. Related work (this part): Non-identifiability (Méloux et al. [6]) — behaviours need not have unique mechanistic explanations; paper focuses downstream cost for filing. Faithfulness metric sensitivity (Miller et al. [8]) — ablation-based faithfulness sensitive to researcher choices; a single-axis sensitivity of Miller et al. is extended here into a seven-axis regulatory propagation; Miller’s released library used as instrument (under its definitions). Structure vs function (Bayat Makou et al. [1]) — structurally distinct circuits can implement same computation (W5T: phantom specialisation); motivates using functional measurement to address equivalence-class objections. Variance as estimation (Méloux et al. [7]) — interpretability viewed as estimation with estimator/seed variance; seed variance included as an axis. Auditability (Lan et al. [4], Sharkey et al. [10], Mueller et al. [9]) — prior conflicting conclusions motivate measurement/criteria and need for standardised evaluation/specification for certification. Multiverse method (Steegen et al. [13]; Simonsohn et al. [12] F9A specification curve; Simmons et al. [11]) — adopt multiverse/specification-curve techniques to expose analytic flexibility. Explanation metrics under optimisation pressure (Hsia et al. [3]) — U4J and T9V can be inflated without changing predictions/explanations; both are among the paper’s four metrics; metric-specific discard reporting used to avoid silent pooling.

Specifications admitting no circuit: 8,279 (discard rate ≈52.3%); surviving specs = 7,561. Metric-specific kept counts (out of 3,960 per metric): T9V kept 3,947 (discard 13; discard rate 0.003), H2W kept 1,467 (discard 2,493; 0.630), N6C kept 1,270 (discard 2,690; 0.679), U4J kept 877 (discard 3,083; 0.779). final_notes: Key results: pooled discovered flip F = 0.7316 (CI [0.7247,0.7380]); discovered vs size-matched null 0.7316 vs 0.6774 (R=1,000 multiverses from 32,491 edges). Fixed-size analyses reverse ordering and sharply reduce F: medium 0.2746 vs null 0.4230; coarse 0.2706 vs null 0.3822; pooled fixed-size F ≈ 0.2706 (CI [0.2550,0.2859]). Metric J: mean 0.1396 (CI [0.1377,0.1418]); paper treats metric as largest single lever, subtracting 0.1377 from 0.7316 to give residual ≈ 0.5939 (reported CI 0.5803–0.6063). H4/replicability: pooled per-example agreement 0.6028 → instability 0.3972; gap to claimed flip rate 0.3344 (CI [0.3297,0.3394]); Cohen’s kappa ≈ 0.0146; raw agreement across sizes 0.52–0.92; accuracy 0.51–0.95. Pooled H4 passes but fixed-size decomposition fails (6/10 sizes fail 0.10 threshold; 5 sizes show negative gaps); pooled effect concentrated ~500–2,000 edge band. Instrument limitations: one of seven documented discovery objectives does not run on canonical task (all 220 cells in that arm fail); overall discard rate 52.3%; surviving pool is metric-imbalanced (Table 2 metric rows: 0.003, 0.630, 0.679, 0.779). errors.explanation: The formula k/(2|E|-k) (with |E| fixed) is increasing in k, so a 500-edge circuit must have equal or larger expected random overlap than a 200-edge circuit. Using the paper's number for k=200 (200/(2|E|-200)=0.031) implies |E| ≈ 3325.806; plugging k=500 gives 500/(2|E|-500) ≈ 0.0813 (8.13%), not 0.008 (0.8%). Thus the stated 0.008 contradicts the paper's formula and its 0.031 value.

steps.notes_before: Model & task: GPT-2 small on indirect-object identification. Pre-registration: append-only file; abstracts drafted in advance. Grid (Section 6): 7 discovery objectives, 7 ablation operators, 4 corruption distributions (nested within 5 operators), 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompt variants, 5 seeds. Section 6 reports this pre-registered design yields 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 specifications. One objective failed completely (all 220 of its cells), so the realised grid has 6 objectives, 1,320 cells and 15,840 specifications (12 specs/cell; 3,960 specs/metric). Statistics: no p-values across specs; nonparametric bootstrap resampling of specifications with B=10,000. Two exclusions (decided before any circuit seen): (1) failed objective (220 cells) removed; (2) metric-relative threshold rule admitted no circuit for 8,279 of 15,840 specs (discard rate 52.3%), leaving 7,561 kept (~47.7%). Table 2 kept/discarded by metric: comprehensiveness 3,947 kept /13 discarded (rate 0.003); KL 1,467/2,493 (0.630); logit diff 1,270/2,690 (0.679); sufficiency 877/3,083 (0.779). Surviving composition: 52% comprehensiveness vs 25% by design. Internal inconsistency noted: earlier part/notes claimed pre-registered total was 15,840, but Section 6 states pre-registered was 18,480 and 15,840 is post-failure realised total.

H4 (pooled): per-example functional agreement ≈0.6028 → instability ≈0.3972; gap to claim flip = 0.3344 (95% CI [0.3297, 0.3394]) > 0.10, so H4 supported pooled but qualified by failures at 6 of 10 sizes and negative gaps at 5 sizes; pooled H4 signal mainly driven by 500–2,000 edge band. Model/task: GPT-2 small, indirect-object identification. Pre-registered 1,320-cell factorial grid; realized 15,840 specs; metric threshold kept 7,561 (~47.7%), discard rate 52.3%; 3,218 distinct circuits; Jaccard over 28,580,580 pairs. Key confirmatory results: P0 holds (mean J̄ = 0.1396, 95% CI [0.1377, 0.1418]). H2: pooled discovered flip F = 0.7316 (95% CI [0.7247, 0.7380]); pooled null F = 0.6774 (randomized multiverses R=1,000 from 32,491 edges). H3: rejected as pooled direction is driven by circuit-size confounding — holding size fixed reverses ordering (medium: discovered ≈0.2746 vs null 0.4230; coarse: 0.2706 vs 0.3822); fixing size drops F from 0.7316 to 0.2746. Table 7: null predictions collapse to one class at ≥1,000 edges (null F = 0.0000); discovered collapse at 5,000 and 10,000 edges (n=625 and 2,067; F = 0.0000) → 2,692 specs produce no flips. H4 (pooled): per-example agreement ≈0.6028 → instability ≈0.3972; gap to claim flip = 0.3344 (95% CI [0.3297, 0.3394]) > 0.10, but fails in many size-specific analyses (6/10 sizes fail; 5 sizes show negative gaps); pooled H4 mainly driven by 500–2,000 edge band. Agreement/accuracy ranges: raw agreement ≈0.60 (size-specific 0.52–0.92); accuracy 0.51–0.95. Filability protocol (new): must declare spec space S and deterministic claim map φ (code), compute π* = max_c n_c/N and F; claim filable if π* ≥ 1−α; filer must report π*, F, discard rates by axis level, and within-group decompositions; filings that cannot state π* treated as assertions. Limitations (this part): one model/one task (Pythia-160m 924-cell replication pre-registered but unrun); circuit size is an outcome that distorts pooled stats; instrument omits optimal ablation [5]; discards are high and metric-imbalanced (metric rows: 0.003, 0.630, 0.679, 0.779); bootstrap invalid for small conditioning groups (2–5 specs) so point estimates reported.

steps.notes_before: Model/task: GPT-2 small, indirect-object identification. Pre-registered 1,320-cell grid; realized 15,840 specs; threshold kept 7,561 (~47.7%), discard 52.3%; 3,218 distinct circuits; Jaccard over 28,580,580 pairs. H3: size confounds pooled effect—holding size fixed drops F to ≈0.2746 (medium discovered 0.2746 vs null 0.4230; coarse 0.2706 vs 0.3822). Table 7: prediction collapse at high edge counts (null F=0.0000 ≥1,000 edges; discovered collapse at 5,000/10,000 edges → 2,692 specs produce no flips). Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Pre-registered crossed design using published implementations to discover circuits for GPT-2 small on indirect object identification. Deterministic code converts discovered circuits into structured Annex IV statements. 7,561 claim-producing specifications; pairwise claim disagreement = 0.7316. "No single-axis standardisation permits filing under the registered tolerances." Removing size from statements and conditioning comparisons on size reduces disagreement to 0.2706. Discovered circuits outperform size-matched randomness at fixed size, reversing the pooled comparison; functional measurements do not support treating circuits as interchangeable mechanisms. Size conditioning also qualifies the pooled functional-gap result. Study covers one model and one task; a committed second-model study remains unrun.

Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Pre-registered crossed design for GPT-2 small (Q7V) on indirect-object identification (Z4K); committed but unrun second-model plan: Pythia-160m (M9B). final_notes: Reproducibility: preregistration commit 'prereg-p1-confirmatory' before confirmatory sweep. Authors claim one environment across all 1,320 cells; content-addressed archive recovered code commit (22/22 files identical). Analysis layer runs without GPU. Verification: a script recomputes headline quantities (36 checks, 0 failures); F derived by three routes including brute-force pairwise. A second script is said to check every numeric token and tables are emitted from stored results; test suite contains 343 tests. Key reported results to track: P0 mean J = 0.1396 [0.1377,0.1418]; H2 pooled discovered F = 0.7316 [0.7247,0.7380]; random-null pooled F = 0.6774. H4 summary: per-example functional agreement ≈0.6028 (instability ≈0.3972); pooled gap to claim flip rate ≈0.3344 [0.3297,0.3394]; pooled Cohen's kappa ≈0.0146; effect concentrated in 500–2,000 edge band. Other protocol notes: instrument omits at least one defensible operator (measured F is a lower bound). Overall discard rate = 52.3%; one exported discovery objective reportedly failed on canonical task with all 220 cells in that arm discarded. Bootstrap CIs unreliable in small conditioning groups (2–5 specs); authors report point estimates with diagnostics but no post-hoc bias correction. Important open inconsistency: H3 text numbers conflict with Table 7 (see above), which directly contradicts the claim that every numeric token/table was exhaustively checked/generated.

Context: confirmatory study on GPT-2 small (indirect object identification). Grid/multiverse: N = 15,840 specifications. 7,561 specifications produce a claim (~47.7%).

Claims & mapping: deterministic claim map φ maps each discovered circuit to a structured Annex IV statement (three nested granularities: COARSE, MEDIUM, FINE). Two claim maps: φ_overseer and φ_affected. Modal claim share π* = max_c n_c / N = 0.411 (≈6,516 specs).

Main reported statistics: claim flip rate F = 73.2% (probability two distinct specifications yield different statements). Standardising the evaluation metric reduces F to 59.4%. Removing circuit size from the claim (holding size fixed) reduces F to 27.1%. Median circuit Jaccard overlap = 4%. Functional agreement (Cohen’s kappa adjusted) ≈ 0; functional instability ≈ 1. Functional gap = F − functional instability.

Method/choices: Seven discovery objectives documented, six executed. Circuit = subset of model edges; component = attention head or MLP. Evaluation metrics include KL/logit diff/sufficiency, accuracy, comprehensiveness. Structural variance: REML decomposition on log10(selected circuit size). Calibration rule maps node-count curve to size bins (labels: sparse/moderate/distributed). Bootstrap: B = 10,000 resamples of specifications (CIs conditional on grid). Random-null multiverses: R = 1,000.

Pre-registered outcomes: H2 (F > 0.20 with CI lower bound > 0.20), H3 (not separated from random null), H4 (F − (1 − agreement) > 0.10). Filability: evidence filable at tolerance α iff π* ≥ 1 − α.

Pre-registered crossed grid (7 discovery axes); 15,840 analytic specifications; deterministic maps φ_overseer and φ_affected. 7,561 specs produced a claim (~47.7%). Specification tuple s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). Discovery returns C(s)⊆E; |E|=32,491 edges (factorised q/k/v). Independent component count: 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 components; text also cites 157 non-terminal sources. Circuit instability D(s_i,s_j)=1−|C_i∩C_j|/|C_i∪C_j| (mean Jaccard = J̄); circuits structurally near-disjoint (median pairwise Jaccard overlap ≈4%). Claim instability: F = 1 − ∑_c n_c(n_c−1) / [N(N−1)] (Gini–Simpson; unit tests vs brute-force). Modal share π* = max_c n_c/N. Conditional within-group flip F_within(G) defined and reduces to Eq.2 when G empty. Filability: evidence filable iff π* ≥ 1−α. Ceiling for F is 1−1/k (k = number of claim classes); with k=9 ceiling = 0.8889; observed F ≈0.7316 (≈0.732), which is 82.3% of ceiling. Reported results: overall F=0.7316 (95% CI [0.725,0.738]); π*≈0.411 (~6,516 specs) failing filability; standardising evaluation metric reduces F→0.594; holding circuit size fixed / removing size from claims reduces F→0.2746 (95% CI [0.255,0.286]); fixed-size discovered vs random flip 0.2746 vs 0.4230. steps.notes_before: Dataset: 7,561 specifications, 3,218 distinct circuits, 28,580,580 spec pairs; pair disagreement 73.2% (95% CI ≈ 0.725–0.738). D quantiles: 1% 0.196, 25% 0.788, median 0.960, 75% 0.998. Median shared-edge fraction ≈4% (≈45× random overlap). Claim-class counts: top 3,107 (41.09%), second 2,153 (28.48%). Size-aggregated early/mid/late: 47.9% / 8.5% / 43.6% (max π* ≈ 0.479). Degeneracy notes: discovered F hits 0 only at 5,000 and 10,000 edges (625+2,067=2,692 specs); earlier textual/table inconsistencies flagged (degeneracy/location claims). Comparative pooled metrics: pooled discovered F=0.7316 vs A6N 0.6774; fixed-size reverses ordering for some families (K8Z fixed-size F=0.2746 vs comparator 0.4230; E7R fixed-size F=0.2706 vs comparator 0.3822). Functional diagnostics: pooled per-example agreement 0.6028 → pooled functional instability 0.3972; pooled Cohen's κ ≈0.0146; within-size κ 0.016–0.047; raw agreement 0.52→0.92; accuracy 0.51→0.95; sizes failing gap threshold 6/10; pooled gap band 500–2,000 edges. Part 15 (Discussion) adds: Table 6 best residual F=0.5939 (95% CI 0.5803–0.6063; 59.4%); claims single-axis standardisation insufficient; instrument/tooling problems documented and publicly exported; asserts "Grid consequence" shows 220 failed objective cells, 8,279 specs admitting no circuit and 52.3% discard rate (this conflicts with total-specs=7,561); Section 7.5 comparison reported fixed-size K8Z 0.2746 vs random 0.4230 and E7R 0.2706 vs random 0.3822; measurement asserted cheap vs discovery. Limitations: one-model run, second-model grid unexecuted; circuit size is outcome not axis and conditioning on size reduces instability more than any single-axis standardisation (fixed-size F=0.2706 vs Table 6 smallest residual F=0.5939); multiverse limited to library (C4Y unsupported → measured F is lower bound); high/uneven discard rates and bootstrap caveats.

grade.reason: Review item 0 identifies the paper's universal claim that every pre-registered specification yielded evidence and notes a contradicted statement that at least one pre-registered objective arm failed and therefore produced no evidence, which matches the planted error's contradiction.

errors.claim: "Note the ceiling: F\leq 1-1/k for k claim classes, so a reported flip rate must be read against the number of classes the map can produce. With the nine classes observed here the ceiling is 0.8889, and the observed 0.7316 is 82.3% of it. F is not near one by construction."
errors.evidence: "Equation 2: F = 1 - \frac{\sum_{c} n_{c}(n_{c}-1)}{N(N-1)}" (the finite-sample Gini–Simpson form) and the quoted ceiling sentence above.
errors.explanation: The displayed formula for F is the without-replacement (finite-sample) form; in fact F = (N/(N-1))*(1 - \sum_c p_c^2). The maximum over distributions p_c (uniform p_c=1/k) gives F_max = (N/(N-1))*(1 - 1/k), which can exceed 1 - 1/k for finite N (and equals 1 when N=k and each class has n_c=1). Thus the statement "F \le 1-1/k" is mathematically incorrect for the estimator in Eq.2.

final_notes: Key results: pooled claim flip rate F = 0.7316 (95% CI 0.7247–0.7380) over 7,561 specs. Table 6: metric (residual) removes 0.1377 → 0.5939; ablation 0.7014 (−0.0302); discovery 0.7018 (−0.0298); threshold 0.7070 (−0.0246); corruption 0.7092 (−0.0224); prompt 0.7232 (−0.0084); seed 0.7307 (−0.0009). REML on log10(selected circuit size): ablation–corruption interaction explains 78.8% structural variance; residual 11.5%; ablation 4.4%; threshold 4.1%; metric 0.7%. Holding circuit size fixed: pooled F ≈ 0.27 (inconsistency: reported 0.2706 in one place and 0.2746 in limitations). Random-baseline: discovered 0.7316 vs null 0.6774; with size held fixed discovered 0.2746 vs null 0.4230 (medium) and 0.2706 vs 0.3822 (coarse). Per-size (medium) discovered collapses to F=0 at sizes 5k & 10k (2,692 specs zero flips). Per-example functional agreement = 0.6028 (instability 0.3972); gap to claim flip rate = 0.3344 (95% CI 0.3297–0.3394). Cohen's kappa overall 0.0146; per-size kappa 0.016–0.047. Summary: H4 supported on pooled pre-registered quantity, but support disappears when holding size fixed. Filability protocol specified. Limitations: one-model/one-task; second-model replication pre-registered but not run; circuit size is threshold-chosen and distorts pooled quantities; multiverse limited; discard rate 52.3%; metric imbalance; bootstrap intervals invalid for small conditioning groups (2–5 specs) so reported as point estimates with diagnostic; no post-hoc bias-corrected estimator. Reproducibility (this part): preregistered commit prereg-p1-confirmatory; confirmatory sweep ran across 1,320 cells in single environment; 22/22 files identical by content-addressed check; analysis runs without GPU; verification script: 36 checks, 0 failures; F derived by three routes including brute-force; second script claims to check every numeric token; every table emitted from results; test suite 343 tests.

Paper: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Research question: whether mechanistic/circuit discovery evidence is robust to defensible analytic variation (two competent analysts, same system and tool, different defensible settings). Method: pre-registered crossed grid of 7 analytic axes (levels taken from published implementations); mapped each discovered circuit via a deterministic claim map to a structured Annex IV statement. Dataset/experiment: GPT-2 small on an indirect object identification task; 15,840 pre-registered specifications, of which 7,561 produced a claim. Main results: derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs (95% CI 0.725–0.738); modal claim covers 41.1% of the space. Standardising the most influential axis (evaluation metric) yields flip rate 59.4%. Removing circuit size from the claim and holding it fixed yields flip rate 27.1% (95% CI 0.255–0.286), still above the pre-registered threshold (threshold value not given here). Circuits are near-disjoint (median pairwise Jaccard overlap 4%) and functionally uncorrelated (Cohen's kappa 0.015) — authors argue instability is not merely one mechanism restated. They provide a filability criterion/protocol and report one of seven documented discovery objectives fails to execute on the library's canonical task. Study limitation: single model and single task; generalisability untested.

final_notes: Paper: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Mahale, 2026). Design/data: discovery grid = 1,540 cells; pre-registered specs 18,480; realized specs 15,840. Specs admitting no circuit = 8,279; surviving (claim-producing) specs = 7,561 (all pairs = 28,580,580). Distinct circuits = 3,218. D metric quantiles (1%,25%,50%,75%) = (0.196,0.788,0.960,0.998). Median shared-edge fraction ~4%; median circuit size 200; analytic random overlap ≈0.0031 at median. Instability: pair disagreement 73.2% (95% CI 0.725–0.738); modal-class share π* = 0.4109; J6D mean J̄ = 0.1396 [0.1377,0.1418]; pooled discovered F = 0.7316 [0.7247,0.7380]. Axis effects (axis-standardised residual F): Evaluation metric 0.5939 (95% CI 0.5803–0.6063), Ablation operator 0.7014, Discovery objective 0.7018, Threshold 0.7070, Corruption 0.7092, Prompt 0.7232, Seed 0.7307. REML structural variance: ablation–corruption interaction 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric 0.7%. Metric-standardised % disagreement 59.4%. Size-free (fixed-size-claim) F = 0.2706 (95% CI 0.2550–0.2859). Random baselines and collapse points reported. Functional diagnostics: per-example agreement 0.6028, smallest-circuit instability 0.4777, Cohen's kappa 0.0146. Y3W filing protocol defined. Limitations: one model/task only; unrun second-model plan M9B (Pythia-160m) uses 924-cell grid; circuit size treated as outcome; C4Y excluded from instrument; high/uneven discard; bootstrap invalid for one reported family so some intervals replaced by point estimates. Reproducibility: public commit tag prereg-p1-confirmatory; archive verification across 1,320 confirmatory cells; content-addressed check recovered commit (22/22 files identical); analysis needs no GPU. Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability. Author: Ajay Pravin Mahale. Date: 12 Aug 2026. Domain: circuit-level interpretability. Main claim (from preface): circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across plausibly acceptable tolerances: competent analysts using the same system and tool can produce incompatible statements under different defensible settings. Limitation: applicability beyond the single model/task studied remains untested. Introduction notes: auditing framed as requiring two auditors to reach the same conclusion (a commissioning requirement, not an ML definition). Regulatory motivation: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (consolidated text amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, CELEX 02024R1689-20260727; read 11 Aug 2026) asks for “general logic” (Annex IV 2(b)) and measures to facilitate interpretation (2(e)); Article 86(1) asks for clear explanations of the AI system’s role. Mechanistic interpretability (circuit discovery) returns a subgraph said to explain behavior; filing such accounts presumes compatibility between analysts. Study design: pre-registered crossed design using published implementations only; circuits are converted into structured Annex IV statements deterministically. Controls standardize individual axes, remove claim-size dependence, and condition on size. Key reported empirical result: three pooled statistics invert when selected objects differ in size. Paper does not propose improved discovery methods—the objection targets the standard assumed when filing current evidence; uses a standards-body decision rule to measure regulatory-claim movement across defensible specifications.

Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability. Author/date: Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026. Domain: circuit-level (mechanistic) interpretability; regulatory filing focus. Main claim: circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across plausibly acceptable tolerances—competent analysts using the same system and tool can produce incompatible statements under different defensible settings. Limitation: single model/task only; broader applicability untested. Study design: pre-registered crossed design using published implementations only; circuits converted deterministically into structured Annex IV statements. Controls standardize individual axes, remove claim-size dependence, condition on size. Key empirical result noted earlier: three pooled statistics invert when selected objects differ in size. Related work (this part): Non-identifiability (Méloux et al. [6]) — behaviours need not have unique mechanistic explanations; paper focuses downstream cost for filing. Faithfulness metric sensitivity (Miller et al. [8]) — ablation-based faithfulness sensitive to researcher choices; a single-axis sensitivity of Miller et al. is extended here into a seven-axis regulatory propagation; Miller’s released library used as instrument (under its definitions). Structure vs function (Bayat Makou et al. [1]) — structurally distinct circuits can implement same computation (W5T: phantom specialisation); motivates using functional measurement to address equivalence-class objections. Variance as estimation (Méloux et al. [7]) — interpretability viewed as estimation with estimator/seed variance; seed variance included as an axis. Auditability (Lan et al. [4], Sharkey et al. [10], Mueller et al. [9]) — prior conflicting conclusions motivate measurement/criteria and need for standardised evaluation/specification for certification. Multiverse method (Steegen et al. [13]; Simonsohn et al. [12] F9A specification curve; Simmons et al. [11]) — adopt multiverse/specification-curve techniques to expose analytic flexibility. Explanation metrics under optimisation pressure (Hsia et al. [3]) — U4J and T9V can be inflated without changing predictions/explanations; both are among the paper’s four metrics; metric-specific discard reporting used to avoid silent pooling.

final_notes: Model/task: GPT-2 small, indirect-object ID. Design: pre-registered 1,320-cell factorial grid; 15,840 specs realized; 7,561 kept (~47.7%), discards 52.3%; 3,218 distinct circuits; Jaccard computed over 28,580,580 pairs. P0: mean J̄ = 0.1396 (95% CI [0.1377,0.1418]). H2 pooled discovered flip F = 0.7316 (95% CI [0.7247,0.7380]); pooled null F = 0.6774. H3: pooled direction driven by circuit-size confounding — holding size fixed reverses ordering (medium: discovered ≈0.2746 vs null 0.4230; coarse: 0.2706 vs 0.3822); fixing size drops F from 0.7316 to 0.2746. Table 7: null predictions collapse at ≥1,000 edges (null F=0.0000); discovered collapse at 5,000 & 10,000 edges (n=625, 2,067) → 2,692 specs with no flips. H4 pooled: per-example agreement ≈0.6028 → instability ≈0.3972; pooled gap to claiming flip = 0.3344 (95% CI [0.3297,0.3394]); many size-specific tests fail (6/10 sizes fail; 5 sizes negative); pooled H4 driven by 500–2,000 edge band. Filability protocol: filer must state spec space S and deterministic claim map φ, compute π* = max_c n_c/N and F; claim filable if π* ≥ 1−α; filings must report π*, F, discard rates, within-group decompositions; filings that cannot state π* are treated as assertions. Limitations: single model/task, omission of optimal ablation, high and metric-imbalanced discards (metric rows 0.003, 0.630, 0.679, 0.779), bootstrap invalid for small conditioning groups so point estimates used. Reproducibility claims (this part): prereg commit tagged 'prereg-p1-confirmatory' made before confirmatory sweep; a single environment was used across all 1,320 cells; archive vs git: 22 of 22 files identical; analysis layer runs without GPU; verification script recomputed every headline quantity (36 checks, 0 failures) and derives F by three routes including brute-force pairwise; second script checks every numeric token; tables emitted from results; test suite contains 343 tests. Note: the paper's Discussion also makes assertions (metric reduces F by 0.1377 to 0.5939, CI 0.5803–0.6063; instability persists across all sizes) that conflict with the size-fixed analyses and Table 7 collapse results recorded above.

Model/task: GPT-2 small, indirect-object identification. Pre-registered 1,320-cell factorial grid; realized 15,840 specs; metric threshold kept 7,561 (~47.7%), discard rate 52.3%; 3,218 distinct circuits; Jaccard over 28,580,580 pairs. Key confirmatory results: P0 holds (mean J̄ = 0.1396, 95% CI [0.1377, 0.1418]). H2: pooled discovered flip F = 0.7316 (95% CI [0.7247, 0.7380]); pooled null F = 0.6774 (randomized multiverses R=1,000 from 32,491 edges). H3: rejected as pooled direction is driven by circuit-size confounding — holding size fixed reverses ordering (medium: discovered ≈0.2746 vs null 0.4230; coarse: 0.2706 vs 0.3822); fixing size drops F from 0.7316 to 0.2746. Table 7: null predictions collapse to one class at ≥1,000 edges (null F = 0.0000); discovered collapse at 5,000 and 10,000 edges (n=625 and 2,067; F = 0.0000) → 2,692 specs produce no flips. H4 (pooled): per-example agreement ≈0.6028 → instability ≈0.3972; gap to claim flip = 0.3344 (95% CI [0.3297, 0.3394]) > 0.10, but fails in many size-specific analyses (6/10 sizes fail; 5 sizes show negative gaps); pooled H4 mainly driven by 500–2,000 edge band. Agreement/accuracy ranges: raw agreement ≈0.60 (size-specific 0.52–0.92); accuracy 0.51–0.95. Filability protocol (new): must declare spec space S and deterministic claim map φ (code), compute π* = max_c n_c/N and F; claim filable if π* ≥ 1−α; filer must report π*, F, discard rates by axis level, and within-group decompositions; filings that cannot state π* treated as assertions. Limitations (this part): one model/one task (Pythia-160m 924-cell replication pre-registered but unrun); circuit size is an outcome that distorts pooled stats; instrument omits optimal ablation [5]; discards are high and metric-imbalanced (metric rows: 0.003, 0.630, 0.679, 0.779); bootstrap invalid for small conditioning groups (2–5 specs) so point estimates reported.

final_notes: Discussion summary: argues for measured evidentiary weight over presumed filing reliability; single-axis standardisation insufficient; instrument execution failure documented (instrument cannot run canonical task); discard rate reflects tooling maturity not headline criticism; interpretability evidence measurable and relatively cheap to acquire. Key diagnostics: Table 6 best residual F = 0.5939 (95% CI 0.5803–0.6063 ≈59.4%); grid: 220 failed-objective cells, 8,279 specs admitting no circuit, 52.3% discard rate. Section 7.5: fixed-size K8Z 0.2746 vs random 0.4230; fixed-size E7R 0.2706 vs random 0.3822. Retained comparisons: pooled Discovered F = 0.7316 vs A6N 0.6774; fixed-size K8Z Discovered 0.2746 vs A6N 0.4230; fixed-size E7R Discovered 0.2706 vs A6N 0.3822. Table 7 (within-size K8Z): size 10 n=2492 D F=0.4543 vs A6N 0.7331; size 1,000 D=0.5133 vs A6N=0.0000; size 2,000 D=0.5714 vs A6N=0.0000; sizes 5k/10k both 0.0000. Agreement/instability: pooled per-example agreement 0.6028 (instability 0.3972); smallest-circuit instability 0.4777; Cohen's kappa 0.0146; raw agreement range 0.52–0.92; accuracy 0.51–0.95; 6/10 sizes fail gap threshold; 5 sizes show negative gap. Limitations: one model/one task; planned second-model 924-cell grid unrun; circuit size treated as outcome not axis; measured space excludes some defensible choices so measured F is a lower bound; bootstrap invalid for one family and some intervals replaced by point estimates. Reproducibility (new): public tagged commit `prereg-p1-confirmatory`; archive verification establishes one environment across all 1,320 confirmatory cells; content-addressed comparison: 22/22 files identical; analysis needs no GPU; one script recomputes headline quantities (36 checks, 0 failures; F checked three ways including brute-force pairs); another checks every manuscript numeric token; tables emitted directly; test suite contains 343 tests.

Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Pre-registered crossed design using published implementations to discover circuits for GPT-2 small on indirect object identification. Deterministic code converts discovered circuits into structured Annex IV statements. 7,561 claim-producing specifications; pairwise claim disagreement = 0.7316. "No single-axis standardisation permits filing under the registered tolerances." Removing size from statements and conditioning comparisons on size reduces disagreement to 0.2706. Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Pre-registered crossed design for GPT-2 small (Q7V) on indirect-object identification (Z4K); committed but unrun second-model plan: Pythia-160m (M9B). Deterministic code G7U maps discovered circuits to structured Annex IV statements; 7,561 claim-producing specifications; pairwise claim disagreement F = 0.7316 (pooled). Removing size from statements and conditioning on size reduces disagreement to 0.2706. Discovered circuits outperform size-matched random null (A6N) at fixed size; pooled comparison reverses. Graph: factorised (query/key/value) with |E| = 32,491 edges; 12 blocks, 12 heads/block (144 heads), 12 MLPs. Specification s = (objective o, ablation operator a, corruption distribution d, metric m, size threshold τ, prompt variant P, seed r, granularity g). Ablation operators: 7 total (five read corruption, two do not); d nested within operators that read corruption. Granularities: COARSE (E7R), MEDIUM (K8Z), FINE (V2H). Metrics (four): comprehensiveness (T9V), KL divergence (H2W), logit difference (N6C), sufficiency (U4J). Discovery: crossed grid, discovery cell counted before metric/threshold/statement reporting; metric-relative threshold rule; retention/discard rates tracked; one objective arm failed (MSE/integral target runtime error). Statistical tooling: Jaccard α = intersection/union, α-bar = mean over unordered pairs; D = 1 - Jaccard; F defined in Gini–Simpson form (pair disagreement); G and F_within(G) for conditioning; pi* = max_class_share; Y3W filability requires pi* >= 1 - alpha (alpha = filing tolerance). Nulls: R = 1,000 null multiverses; null degeneracy = collapse. Inference: bootstrap B = 10,000 resamples of specifications; pairwise U-statistics for F and α-bar; p-values not reported (grid not independent). Functional diagnostics: agreement, functional instability = 1 - agreement, functional gap = F - (1 - agreement), Cohen's kappa, accuracy. Structural variance: REML over log10(size). Discovery families: edge-attribution patching (R8X), integrated edge gradients (B3Q); optimal ablation (C4Y) unsupported. Pre-registration artifacts: deviations file, six-cell validation slice, environment fingerprint, content-addressed git tree, tag 'prereg-p1-confirmatory'. GPU not required.

Contributions: measure filing instability; test whether standardisation or size explains it; use published implementations exclusively; deterministic mapping to Annex IV; controls standardise analytic axes, remove claim dependence on size, and condition comparisons on size; three pooled statistics (calculated before size conditioning) invert when selected objects differ in size. No new discovery method proposed; the objection targets the filing standard, not interpretability’s value.

Repro claims: preregistered commit prereg-p1-confirmatory; confirmatory sweep across 1,320 cells under single environment; code commit matched 22/22 files; analysis layer runs without a GPU; verification scripts: 36 checks 0 failures and a second script that purportedly checks every numeric token; test suite 343 tests. Limitations: one model/task, secondary replication limited, circuit size is an outcome (selection distorts pooled stats), multiverse limited, discard rate 52.3%, metric-imbalanced.

Study: circuit-level interpretability reliability for indirect-object-identification in GPT-2 small. Pre-registered multiverse was earlier described as 7 analytic axes and 15,840 pre-registered specs, but an earlier part defined the specification tuple s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g) (8 axes) — inconsistency previously flagged. Circuit instability metric: D = 1 − |C_i ∩ C_j| / |C_i ∪ C_j| (Jaccard); mean Jaccard reported. Claim-map φ: pre-registered, deterministic code (not LLM-generated). Two addressees: φ_overseer (keyed: dominant layer band → size class → ranked input segment; built on Annex IV/Article 14 refs) and φ_affected (leads with input segment; built on Article 86(1)). Three granularities are nested by construction. Claim-instability metrics: flip F = 1 − ∑_c n_c(n_c−1) / (N(N−1)) (Gini–Simpson); modal share π* = max_c n_c / N; filability iff π* ≥ 1−α. Ceiling F ≤ 1−1/k with k=9 → 0.8889; observed F≈0.7316 (~82.3% of ceiling). Size distribution drives the pooled direction: holding size fixed reverses ordering — medium granularity discovered F=0.2746 vs null 0.4230; coarse discovered F=0.2706 vs null 0.3822. Section 8 defines a filability protocol. Key steps: (1) declare the specification space S (analytic axes and defensible levels, with citations); (2) declare the claim map φ as deterministic, published code (explicitly: not a language model); (3) compute π* = max_c n_c / N over S, and compute F using Equation 2 (F is the flip rate defined earlier); (4) a claim is filable at tolerance α if π* ≥ 1 − α; (5) report π*, F, discard rate by axis level, and the within-group decomposition of any pooled statistic. The text emphasizes that a filing that cannot state its π* is an assertion, not an audit, and that the regulator need not pick the correct analytic choice — the filer must declare the space and report how much of it agrees. (Retain prior Section 7 summary: pooled F ≈ 0.7316, J-bar ≈ 0.1396, per-size reversals and per-size stats — filability uses π* and F from those computations.)

Section 8 filability protocol: (1) declare specification space S (analytic axes and defensible levels); (2) declare claim map φ as deterministic, published code (explicitly not an LLM); (3) compute π* = max_c n_c / N over S and compute F via Eq.2; (4) claim filable at tolerance α if π* ≥ 1 − α; (5) report π*, F, discard rate by axis level, and within-group decompositions. Prior pooled results referenced: pooled F ≈ 0.7316, J̄ ≈ 0.1396; per-size reversals and per-size stats feed filability decisions. Section 9 limitations (this part): generalisation untested — one model & one task; a 924-cell Pythia-160m replication (pre-registered) is unrun (seeds: 3 levels vs original 5), and a second task is designed but unrun. Circuit size is an outcome (threshold rule selects size) and distorts three pooled quantities; fixing size reduces F from 0.7316 to 0.2746 and changes direction/sign of some comparisons; authors report pooled stats with within-size decomposition. Multiverse equals implemented library, not entire literature: optimal ablation [5] omitted, so measured F is a lower bound vs full defensible operator set. Discard rate high: overall 52.3%; surviving pool metric-imbalanced with metric-row rates reported (Table 2): 0.003, 0.630, 0.679, 0.779. Bootstrap invalid for some conditioning families (groups of 2–5 specs dominated by retained self-pairs); paper reports point estimates + diagnostics and did not adopt a bias-corrected estimator after seeing naive intervals disagree.

errors.claim: The metric is the biggest lever. It removes 0.1377 from a 0.7316 flip rate.
errors.location: this part (Section 10) vs earlier notes (limitations / Section 9)

final_notes: Key results: pooled pair-disagreement F = 0.7316; preregistered modal-share filing threshold π* ≥ 0.80. Specs: 7,561 claim-producing specs, 3,218 distinct circuits, 28,580,580 spec pairs. Structural diagnostics: median D = 0.960, median shared-edge fraction 4%, median circuit size k = 200; analytic random baseline at k=200 = 0.0031. Most-common claim share ≈ 0.4109. Metric standardisation removes 0.1377 leaving residual F = 0.5939 (Table 6; 95% CI 0.5803–0.6063; percent 59.4%). REML (log10 size) variance decomposition: ablation×corruption 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric 0.7%. Size-free (fixed-size) claim F = 0.2706 (95% CI 0.2550–0.2859) > preregistered 0.20. Functional diagnostics: pooled per-example agreement 0.6028 (instability 0.3972); smallest-circuit instability 0.4777; Cohen’s κ = 0.0146; within-size κ 0.016–0.047; raw agreement range 0.52–0.92; accuracy range 0.51–0.95. Instrumenting/tooling: 220 failed objective cells, 8,279 specs admitting no circuit, grid-discard rate 52.3%; Table 2 discard rates 0.003, 0.630, 0.679, 0.779. Discovered circuits retain signal (Section 7.5): fixed-size K8Z 0.2746 vs random 0.4230; fixed-size E7R 0.2706 vs random 0.3822. Protocol Y3W proposed; limitations include one model/task run, circuit size as outcome (conditioning affects F), limited multiverse, high/uneven discard, and one invalid bootstrap family for tiny groups. Reproducibility: public commit tag prereg-p1-confirmatory; archive verification establishes one environment across all 1,320 confirmatory cells; content-addressed comparison finds 22/22 files identical; analysis needs no GPU. One script recomputes headline quantities: 36 checks, 0 failures, F checked via three routes including brute-force pairs. Another script checks every manuscript numeric token; tables emitted directly. Test suite contains 343 tests.

Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Pre-registered crossed design using published implementations to discover circuits for GPT-2 small on indirect object identification. Deterministic code converts discovered circuits into structured Annex IV statements. 7,561 claim-producing specifications; pairwise claim disagreement = 0.7316. "No single-axis standardisation permits filing under the registered tolerances." Removing size from statements and conditioning comparisons on size reduces disagreement to 0.2706. Discovered circuits outperform size-matched randomness at fixed size, reversing the pooled comparison; functional measurements do not support treating circuits as interchangeable mechanisms. Size conditioning also qualifies the pooled functional-gap result. Study covers one model and one task; a committed second-model study remains unrun.

Title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability (Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026). Pre-registered crossed design for GPT-2 small (Q7V) on indirect-object identification (Z4K); committed but unrun second-model plan: Pythia-160m (M9B). Deterministic code G7U maps discovered circuits to structured Annex IV statements; 7,561 claim-producing specifications; pairwise claim disagreement F = 0.7316 (pooled). Removing size from statements and conditioning on size reduces disagreement to 0.2706. Discovered circuits outperform size-matched random null (A6N) at fixed size; pooled comparison reverses. Graph: factorised (query/key/value) with |E| = 32,491 edges; 12 blocks, 12 heads/block (144 heads), 12 MLPs. Specification s = (objective o, ablation operator a, corruption distribution d, metric m, size threshold τ, prompt variant P, seed r, granularity g). Ablation operators: 7 total (five read corruption, two do not); d nested within operators that read corruption. Granularities: COARSE (E7R), MEDIUM (K8Z), FINE (V2H). Metrics (four): comprehensiveness (T9V), KL divergence (H2W), logit difference (N6C), sufficiency (U4J). Discovery: crossed grid, discovery cell counted before metric/threshold/statement reporting; metric-relative threshold rule; retention/discard rates tracked; one objective arm failed (MSE/integral target runtime error). Statistical tooling: Jaccard α = intersection/union, α-bar = mean over unordered pairs; D = 1 - Jaccard; F defined in Gini–Simpson form (pair disagreement); G and F_within(G) for conditioning; pi* = max_class_share; Y3W filability requires pi* >= 1 - alpha (alpha = filing tolerance). Nulls: R = 1,000 null multiverses; null degeneracy = collapse. Inference: bootstrap B = 10,000 resamples of specifications; pairwise U-statistics for F and α-bar; p-values not reported (grid not independent). Functional diagnostics: agreement, functional instability = 1 - agreement, functional gap = F - (1 - agreement), Cohen's kappa, accuracy. Structural variance: REML over log10(size). Discovery families: edge-attribution patching (R8X), integrated edge gradients (B3Q); optimal ablation (C4Y) unsupported. Pre-registration artifacts: deviations file, six-cell validation slice, environment fingerprint, content-addressed git tree, tag 'prereg-p1-confirmatory'. GPU not required.
